The curriculum, developed by a world-class faculty of scholars and practitioners, trains the next generation of leaders and professionals to bridge the gap between scientific knowledge and practical application. Students learn to think in a systems-based, holistic way and to address the social, economic and environmental aspects of any challenge. The program prepares graduates who can create and implement sustainability solutions in a wide range of contexts.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Sustainability,
Department: School of Sustainability
Concentration: ['Ecosystems sustainability', 'Policy and governance in sustainable systems', 'Sustainable energy, materials and technology', 'Sustainable food systems', 'Urban sustainability']
Description:
The Master of Science in sustainability is a research-oriented degree program in the School of Sustainability. The program provides students with a substantive, transdisciplinary education in sustainability and problem-solving, with a focus on conducting research. The MS program culminates in a thesis or a capstone in the form of a publishable paper.

The curriculum includes a core of three required courses along with a set of methods courses and electives to complement the thesis or capstone project. Students learn from a renowned community of sustainability scholars and scientists and gain invaluable experience from the research they conduct. Each student also works with a faculty mentor for guidance.

Students in the Master of Science program select one of five tracks:
Ecosystems sustainability
Policy and governance in sustainable systems
Sustainable energy, materials and technology
Sustainable food systems
Urban sustainability

The MS in sustainability program is ideal for students who are interested in a research-based career and for graduates who go on to pursue a doctoral degree.
ScholarshipType: Scholarships, fellowships, teaching assistantships, research assistantships

ProgramName: Sustainability, PhD
Requirements:
Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the College of Global Futures.

Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in any field from a regionally accredited institution.

Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in an applicable master's degree program.

All applicants must submit:

1. graduate admission application and application fee
2. official transcripts
3. resume or curriculum vitae
4. statement of purpose
5. three letters of recommendation
6. proof of English proficiency
Department: School of Sustainability
Concentration: Urban sustainability, Ecosystem sustainability, Policy and governance in sustainable systems, Social transformations in sustainability, Sustainable energy, materials and technology
Description:
The PhD program in sustainability prepares the next generation of scholar-activists to understand, research and develop solutions for the complex environmental, economic, social and cultural challenges of the 21st century. The curriculum provides a broad understanding of the concepts and methods of sustainability and an in-depth understanding of one or more related fields. The program promotes interdisciplinary connections with other ASU schools and departments. Graduates of this program are well prepared for a wide variety of careers in academia, government and industry.

The degree program offers five unique tracks:

Urban sustainability
Ecosystem sustainability
Policy and governance in sustainable systems
Social transformations in sustainability
Sustainable energy, materials and technology

Each of these tracks provides a lens through which students can view the world's pressing sustainability problems and potential solutions, as well as a focus from which to structure their own coursework, research and dissertation.

The program encourages students to move beyond the traditional academic disciplines to gain a deeper understanding of the complex interactions of human and natural systems. Sustainability scholars are problem-solvers who can cross traditional academic boundaries, integrate different kinds of knowledge, and link scholarship to real-world engagement.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Sustainable Engineering,
Department: School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment
Description:
The MS program in sustainable engineering is a transdisciplinary graduate degree program dedicated to addressing complex environmental, societal and economic problems. Students learn the tools of sustainability science and engineering with the goal of ensuring future human well-being and protecting the quality of life, the natural resource base and the ecological systems of the planet.

Students are educated on critical concepts and methods, such as:
- circular economy
- earth systems engineering and management
- industrial ecology
- life cycle assessment
- pollution prevention and control
- sustainable development
- systems thinking

The program provides a broad education through its core courses, while also allowing students to specialize through technical electives. Students can complete a thesis or a nonthesis option. The nonthesis option requires an applied project.

ProgramName: Systems Engineering, PhD
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The systems engineering PhD program is for students who want to develop a fundamental understanding of systems theories and methodologies in order to address complex, real-world engineering and socio-technical problems.

The doctoral program in systems engineering provides the skills and knowledge necessary to perform advanced research in specialized areas of systems engineering and to successfully pursue research and development careers in academia, industry and government. The curriculum allows students to gain a strong foundation in the concepts of systems engineering and also provides flexibility for students to pursue their own research interests. Under the guidance of a faculty advisor, students choose electives in a specialized area that prepares them for dissertation research. The core coursework consists of a common set of subjects related to the fundamentals of systems engineering, and the program culminates with a dissertation that demonstrates a significant and original contribution to the field.

ProgramName: Teaching, MEd
Requirements:
Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College.

Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in any field from a regionally accredited institution.

Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in an applicable master's degree program.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The MEd program in teaching is a graduate-level program that leads to a recommendation for an initial Arizona teaching certificate in secondary or elementary education.

This master's degree program is designed for students with a bachelor's degree in a field other than education who want to pursue a career in teaching. The program offers secondary education certification in the content areas of English, history, mathematics, political science or science (biology, chemistry, earth and space science, general science or physics). The program also offers elementary education certification for grades K–8.

Students work in collaborative cohorts with a group of approximately 25 students. Faculty members work with these small groups to provide an intensive, high-quality learning experience. The programs for both elementary and secondary education certification consist of a combination of coursework and a full-time, yearlong residency in a K–12 school. Upon completion of the program, students earn their master's degree and a recommendation for an Arizona teaching certificate.

The secondary education certification program places an emphasis on preparing teachers to work with the diverse student populations typically found in middle school and high school settings in Arizona. The elementary education certification program places an emphasis on preparing teachers to work with the diverse student populations typically found in K–8 school settings in Arizona.
Accredidation: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the American Psychological Association and the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages, MTESOL
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages program provides students with a strong foundation in the theory and practice of second language teaching, learning and assessment. The degree prepares graduates for a wide range of English language teaching positions in the U.S. and abroad, including teaching in:

community language programs
immigrant and refugee resettlement organizations
private language schools
K-12 school systems (with appropriate state certification)
community colleges
universities
a variety of institutions abroad

Students learn from and collaborate with world-class faculty in the Department of English and have the opportunity to participate in cutting-edge research in linguistics and applied linguistics. Students are also supported in pursuing professional development opportunities like presenting at academic conferences and getting involved in professional organizations.

This program is offered by the Department of English, an academic unit of The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, and is one of the largest and most productive English departments in the U.S. The department is home to more than 300 award-winning faculty members who are national and international leaders in their fields.

ASU is a broadly diverse, service-oriented and community-engaged university. U.S. News & World Report has ranked ASU No. 1 among the Most Innovative Schools in America for the ninth consecutive year, and it is the highest-ranked university in the U.S. for innovation.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre,
Requirements:
Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts.

Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in theatre or a related field from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program, or applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in an applicable master's degree program.

Required application materials:

*   graduate admission application and application fee
*   official transcripts
*   statement of purpose
*   three letters of recommendation
*   proof of English proficiency
*   resume or curriculum vitae
*   a portfolio and an interview with the faculty

Applicants must submit contact information for three recommenders. The recommenders will be sent an email with a link to upload their letter of recommendation.
Department: Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, School of Music, Dance and Theatre
Concentration: ['Directing', 'Interdisciplinary Digital Media and Performance', 'Performance', 'Theatre for Youth and Community']
Description:
The MFA in theatre is a terminal degree and provides students the opportunity to specialize in one of three areas of study: acting, directing, or theatre for youth and community. Students work in a conservatory environment within a large research university.

The program emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical application, providing a variety of opportunities to apply students' learning and skills in production, including mainstage shows, student-directed projects, new work development, and work in the community.

The acting program is a three-year, 60-credit-hour program with a focus on stage, film and television acting and preparation for a career in the professional world.

The directing program has an international reputation for its focus on new work and new ways of working and for its focus on director-designer collaboration. Graduates of the program are working on Broadway, in major regional theatres, in film and television, and at universities around the world.

The theatre for youth and community program is one of the most respected in the U.S. and attracts students from around the world. It provides artists, scholars and educators with a flexible and individualized course of study for creating theatre and community-engaged arts programs with, by and for young people and communities.

The program is flexible and individualized, with students selecting courses and research topics that reflect their interests and career goals. Every student's program of study is unique. Students receive financial support and extensive teaching opportunities and are mentored by a faculty of practicing artists and scholars who are nationally and internationally recognized in their fields.
Accredidation: National Association of Schools of Theatre, Accredited

ProgramName: Urban and Environmental Planning, MUEP
Department: School of Geographical Sciences and Urban Planning, The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description: The Master of Urban and Environmental Planning program in the School of Geographical Sciences and Urban Planning provides students with the background and skills to become professional planners, addressing complex social and environmental issues and planning for more sustainable, equitable, healthy, livable and economically vibrant communities. This is an accredited professional degree that prepares graduates for employment in the public, private and nonprofit sectors. The MUEP program addresses both urban and environmental planning and recognizes the inherent relationship between the two. The curriculum covers a broad range of planning subjects while encouraging depth in a specialization area.
Accredidation: The Master of Urban and Environmental Planning is an accredited program of the Planning Accreditation Board (PAB), the official accrediting agency for master's degree programs in planning in the United States and Canada.

ProgramName: Urban Planning, PhD
Department: School of Geographical Sciences and Urban Planning
Description:
The Doctor of Philosophy program in urban planning is a research-oriented degree. It is designed for students seeking careers in university teaching and research or in policy and research positions in the public, private or nonprofit sectors. The goal of the program is to educate a new generation of scholars and leaders with the substantive knowledge and research skills to address the critical challenges facing urban and metropolitan regions around the world.

The program emphasizes the development of theories, methodologies and their application in urban planning. It provides a strong substantive and methodological foundation, allowing students the flexibility to pursue their own specialized research interests.

Students tailor their programs of study in consultation with their advisors to focus on one of the following areas of interest:

Community development and housing: This area of study is focused on the social, economic and political dynamics of neighborhoods and communities, and their connections with the larger metropolitan area. Students focus on a range of topics including housing policy and finance, community-based planning, social justice, and international development.

Environmental planning: This area of study is focused on the theory and practice of integrating environmental concerns into urban and regional planning. Students focus on a range of topics, including sustainable development, environmental policy and social-ecological systems, water resource management, and climate change planning.

Land use and urban design: This area of study is focused on the built environment and the forces that shape it. Students focus on a range of topics, including land use planning and regulations, urban form and transportation, infill and redevelopment, and planning for healthy communities.

Transportation planning: This area of study is focused on the planning of transportation systems. Students focus on a range of topics, including transportation and land use, transportation policy and finance, transit planning and traffic modeling.

The doctoral curriculum provides students with rigorous training in planning theory, research design and methodology. The program structure offers both breadth in the various subfields of urban planning and depth within a student's particular area of interest, culminating in dissertation research that advances the knowledge of planning. Students will be prepared for successful careers in academia or in high-level policy and research positions where they can effectively address the challenges of planning in today's increasingly complex and globalized world.

ProgramName: Visual Communication Design, Master of Science in Design
Department: Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, The Design School
Description:
The Master of Science in Design with a concentration in visual communication design is a two-year program for students with a background in design who want to elevate their careers and expertise as design leaders and educators.

This program attracts graduate students with a broad range of interests within the visual communication design field, including publication design, exhibition design, human-centered design, information design, interaction design, new media, social design, design research, design strategy and user experience design.

The Master of Science in Design with a concentration in visual communication design is a STEM-designated program. The curriculum focuses on expanding students' expertise and research in a specific area of interest. Coursework emphasizes design research methods and a thesis or applied project that demonstrates a graduate level of inquiry and expertise in a specific area of visual communication design.

As a research university, ASU focuses on expanding design knowledge. Graduate students' individual research pursuits are central to their studies, as is understanding research theory and methods.

The program fosters a small, cohesive student cohort, with faculty who are dedicated to graduate education and work closely with students as mentors. The faculty's diverse interests help students hone their own research interests. Each student is challenged to develop a unique area of specialization to research through their design work and writing.
ScholarshipType: Teaching and research assistantships, tuition scholarships, travel grants

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Accountancy,
Requirements:
The W. P. Carey School of Business has higher admission standards than university admission standards. First-year students are invited to the W. P. Carey School of Business on a competitive, space-available basis. Admission is based on academic achievement in high school.

To be considered for admission to the W. P. Carey School of Business, first-year students must meet the following criteria:

- rank in the top 25% of their high school class OR
- have a 3.00 or higher cumulative GPA (4.00 = "A") OR
- have a 25 or higher ACT score OR
- have a 1230 or higher SAT Reasoning score (critical reading and math only)

Transfer students must have a 3.00 or higher cumulative GPA in all transfer coursework (4.00 = "A") and must have completed 24 or more transferable credit hours post-high school.
Department: W. P. Carey School of Business
Description:
The BS program in accountancy provides a broad-based education in business and a comprehensive education in accounting. The W. P. Carey School of Business accountancy programs are widely recognized for their high-quality instruction and the excellence of their graduates. The programs focus on understanding the role of accounting in society as well as the underlying concepts of accounting. Students are encouraged to develop a sense of inquiry, a desire for lifelong learning and the ability to adapt to a changing professional environment.

Students learn how to provide services that assure the reliability of information and how to design and implement information systems used to generate data for decision-making. Students gain a deeper understanding of areas such as taxation, auditing, financial reporting and management accounting. Because the school attracts many students who have had international experiences, a strong emphasis is placed on preparing students for global business opportunities.

Graduates often begin their careers with professional services firms, in business or in government. Graduates are well prepared to advance quickly in their chosen fields. The BS program in accountancy may be appropriate for students who are not planning to seek professional certification as a CPA. Most states, including Arizona, require 150 semester hours of education for CPA certification. This program requires 120 credit hours.
Accredidation: The accountancy BS program at ASU is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the original 16 schools to have both its business and accounting programs accredited by AACSB International. This represents the highest standard of achievement for business schools worldwide. Programs that earn accreditation confirm their commitment to quality and continuous improvement through a rigorous and comprehensive peer review. Less than five percent of the more than 16,000 business schools worldwide have been accredited.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Science,
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. In addition, new students must meet the following requirements: minimum 1140 SAT combined evidence-based reading and writing plus math score or 22 ACT combined score or 3.00 minimum GPA in ASU competency courses or class ranking in top 25% of high school class. English language proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, etc.) may be required.
Department: School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences
Description:
The BS program in actuarial science provides a strong foundation in mathematics, statistics and business for students interested in a career as an actuarial professional. The program prepares students to pass the initial actuarial exams administered by the Society of Actuaries and the Casualty Actuarial Society.

In addition to fulfilling the mathematics and statistics requirements of the program, students take courses in computer science, economics, finance, accounting and other business areas.

The Society of Actuaries has recognized this program for its quality curriculum, and it is on the society's list of Universities and Colleges with Actuarial Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Management Technology (Air Traffic Management),
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. To be considered for admission, applicants must have successfully completed ASU's competency requirements and meet at least one of the aptitude requirements.

Competency requirements include:
- English (4 years)
- Math (4 years)
- Laboratory Science (3 years)
- Social Science (2 years)
- Second Language (2 years)
- Fine Arts or Career and Technical Education (1 year)

Aptitude requirements (meet at least one):
- Be in the top 25% of your high school graduating class.
- Have a 3.00 or higher GPA (on a 4.00 scale) in your competency courses.
- Have an ACT score of 22 or higher (24 for nonresidents).
- Have an SAT score of 1120 or higher (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description: The aeronautical management technology program at ASU provides a technical foundation in the aviation field with a management focus. The air traffic management concentration prepares students for a career in air traffic control. The curriculum meets the Federal Aviation Administration requirements for graduates of an approved program to be recommended for the Air Traffic-Collegiate Training Initiative. Upon graduation, students may be eligible to bypass the first five weeks of initial qualification training at the FAA Academy. Graduates also may be eligible to take the air traffic selection and training exam earlier than the general public. This is a competitive program; space is limited. Students will spend an average of 15 to 20 hours a week in specialized air traffic control labs.
Accredidation: This program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Management Technology (Air Transportation Management),
Requirements:
First-year applicants must meet ASU's general university admission requirements, which include completion of the following high school competency requirements:

Four years of English (composition and literature)
Four years of math (one year each of algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite)
Three years of lab science (one year each from biology, chemistry, earth science or physics)
Two years of social science (including one year of American history)
Two years of the same second language
One year of fine arts or career and technical education

In addition to the competency requirements, you will need to meet at least one of the following aptitude requirements:

be in the top 25% of their high school graduating class
have a 3.00 cumulative GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A)
have an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents)
have an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The aeronautical management technology program is a management-oriented degree program designed to prepare graduates for a variety of careers in the aviation industry. The program provides students with a strong foundation of aviation knowledge and skills through a multidisciplinary program with a choice of one of three concentrations: air traffic management, air transportation management or professional flight.

The air transportation management concentration curriculum provides a broad perspective of aviation management and operations. The coursework provides a strong business and management foundation applicable to all facets of the aviation industry, from general aviation to commercial air transportation and from civilian to military aviation. The program is specifically designed to prepare graduates for a wide variety of professional careers in the air transportation industry, including airline management and operations, air cargo management and logistics, airport management and operations, corporate aviation management, and government and non-government aviation and aerospace organizations.

Graduates of the air transportation management concentration have a broad understanding of the airline and corporate aviation industries as well as the airport's role within the national airspace system. They are trained in aviation safety, security, operations and management and are prepared for a variety of career paths. Students learn to implement and manage systems that are key to a safe and efficient air transportation system and that move people and goods safely around the world.

The aeronautical management technology program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.
Accredidation: The aeronautical management technology program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Management Technology (Professional Flight),
Requirements:
First-year applicants must meet ASU's general university admission requirements, which includes completion of the ASU competency requirements and one of the following:

- top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
- SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)

ASU competency requirements:

- Four years of math, including algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite.
- Four years of English.
- Three years of lab science, with one year each from chemistry, physics, biology, earth science or an integrated science.
- Two years of social science, including one year of American history.
- Two years of the same second language.
- One year of fine arts or career and technical education.
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The aeronautical management technology program prepares students for a variety of leadership and management positions in the aviation industry. This concentration provides students with the required aeronautical knowledge and skills to earn a commercial pilot certificate with multiengine and instrument ratings.

In addition to general education requirements, students take courses in aviation weather, safety, security, human factors, air traffic control and airport management. The program culminates with two capstone courses in which students solve real-world aviation problems.

Professional flight students can complete their private pilot certificate at a flight provider of their choice before entering the program. Students complete the instrument, commercial, multiengine and certified flight instructor courses with ATP Flight School, ASU's affiliate for flight training. Graduates of the program are eligible for a R-ATP certificate at 1,000 flight hours, per FAA regulations.
Accredidation: The Aeronautical Management Technology (Professional Flight) BS is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Management Technology (Unmanned Aerial Systems),
Requirements:
First-year applicants must meet ASU's general university admission requirements, which include completion of the ASU competency requirements.

First-year applicants must also meet the following admission requirements for this degree program:
- top 25% in high school class OR
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A") OR
- ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents) OR
- SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: The Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The aeronautical management technology program is a management- and business-focused degree for students interested in a broad range of careers in the aerospace industry, both in the flight and in the ground support areas. This program provides students with a strong foundation in technical areas, including:

aircraft flight systems
aircraft propulsion
air traffic control
aviation safety
unmanned aerial systems

The program also develops students' skills in:

aviation law
financial accounting
human factors
leadership
management
marketing

This unique combination of technical and business knowledge prepares graduates for a wide range of leadership roles in the aviation industry.

The unmanned aerial systems concentration provides students with knowledge in all aspects of unmanned aerial systems, including:

design
operations
policy
systems
uses
Accredidation: The aeronautical management technology (unmanned aerial systems) program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.

ProgramName: Aerospace Engineering (Aeronautics), BSE
Requirements:
The Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering have a single admission process for all undergraduate majors. Admission to the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering is based on a student's undergraduate admission application to ASU and the student meeting the following criteria:

First-year student:
- top 25% in high school class, OR
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A"), OR
- ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents), OR
- SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)

English proficiency requirements for international students are the same as the university's.

If a student does not meet the direct admission requirements, the student will be admitted to the Polytechnic School with a major of engineering (exploratory), and through the successful completion of foundational coursework, will be able to declare a specific engineering major.
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The aerospace engineering BSE program with a concentration in aeronautics provides a broad and challenging, high-quality education that prepares students for the practice of engineering at a professional level. The program develops graduates with the technical and critical-thinking skills needed to design aircraft and propulsion systems for commercial and military use.

Students learn from leading experts in aerospace engineering, including five National Academy of Engineering members and 11 fellows of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics. Students can gain a competitive edge through participation in a number of student organizations and research labs.

Aerospace engineers learn the fundamentals of aerodynamics, stability and control, propulsion and structures to design flight vehicles that meet specified performance and safety requirements. The concentration in aeronautics focuses on the design of vehicles that fly within the Earth's atmosphere, such as airplanes, helicopters and unmanned aerial vehicles.
Accredidation: The aerospace engineering BSE program with a concentration in aeronautics is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Aerospace and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Aerospace Engineering (Astronautics), BSE
Department: School for Engineering of Matter, Transport and Energy
Description:
The BSE program in aerospace engineering with a concentration in astronautics provides students with an education in the fundamental principles of aerospace engineering as well as specialized knowledge in the analysis and design of space vehicles and their subsystems. Graduates are well prepared for careers in the aerospace industry or for graduate study.

Aerospace engineering is the branch of engineering that focuses on the design, construction, testing and operation of vehicles that operate in the Earth's atmosphere and in space. Aerospace engineers are employed by the aerospace and defense industries, research and development laboratories and government agencies, and some graduates become astronauts.

Aerospace engineers develop new technologies for use in space exploration, commercial aviation, national defense systems and climate monitoring. They often specialize in one or more areas of aerospace engineering, including:

aerodynamics, the study of how air flows over and around aerospace vehicles and the forces the flow produces

flight mechanics, which is the study of the trajectory and rotational motion of vehicles in the air or in space

flight software and controls, which focuses on the design of the control systems to ensure the desired vehicle performance

propulsion, which is the design of engines and other devices to propel the vehicles in the atmosphere or in space

structural design and analysis, which focuses on the design of the physical configuration of the vehicle to withstand the aerodynamic and other forces to which it is subjected

Students receive a broad education in the fundamental principles of aerospace engineering as well as specialized knowledge in the analysis and design of space vehicles and their subsystems.

The program culminates in a senior-year capstone design experience in which students work in teams to design a complete aerospace vehicle, from initial concept to final design.
Accredidation: The aerospace engineering (astronautics), BSE is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Aerospace and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Aerospace Engineering (Autonomous Vehicle Systems), BSE
Requirements:
To be admitted to this program, you must meet the following requirements in addition to the university's first-year admission requirements:

top 25% in high school class
OR
3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
OR
ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
OR
SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The aerospace engineering BSE program provides students with an education in the fundamental principles of aerospace engineering. The program focuses on developing the knowledge and skills necessary for the design and development of aerospace vehicles and systems. The curriculum offers a balance of theoretical and practical hands-on experiences and addresses the design of aircraft, spacecraft and related systems.

The autonomous vehicle systems concentration provides students the ability to apply fundamental aerospace engineering knowledge to autonomous vehicle systems. In addition to a set of core aerospace engineering courses that provide a strong foundation, the students are required to take a set of courses that offer hands-on experience in autonomous vehicles. Graduates with this concentration are well equipped to work in this fast-growing sector of the economy.

The aerospace engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Accredidation: The aerospace engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African and African American Studies,
Requirements: Arizona State University has a holistic admission process. We look at the whole student when making an admission decision. We consider a variety of factors along with your academic record. Those factors include: course rigor, GPA, standardized test scores (if provided), a personal statement, your high school and community activities. First-year applicants may be admitted to ASU without a test score. If you choose not to submit an ACT or SAT score as part of your application, you will still be considered for admission.
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description: The BA program in African and African American studies is an interdisciplinary degree program in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences that provides a comprehensive, holistic and rigorous introduction to the study of Africa and people of African descent throughout the world. The program aims to expose students to a full range of social, political, cultural and historical subjects, centered on the experiences of people of African descent. Students learn the histories and contemporary experiences of African Americans and other people in the African diaspora, as well as those living on the African continent. Students develop the skills necessary to analyze and evaluate information from a variety of sources and in various forms. They learn to critically examine complex social and historical issues, construct cogent arguments, and communicate their ideas effectively in both writing and speech. The program helps students develop a critical consciousness of the national and global connections relevant to people of African descent. It facilitates an understanding of how race and other socially constructed categories have shaped the lives and experiences of African-descended people. Students learn how to analyze the concepts of race and racism from an interdisciplinary perspective. This includes studying the social and historical contexts in which these ideas have been created and reproduced, how racial identities are constructed and how race continues to be a factor in contemporary society. The program provides students with a general education in the arts, humanities and social sciences. This ensures they acquire a solid foundation in the research and analytical methods used in these broad disciplines and are able to apply them to specific questions and issues. Students leave the program with highly marketable and transferable skills that prepare them for a wide range of careers in both the private and public sectors.
ScholarshipAmount: Varies, e.g., New American University Scholarship for non-residents ranges from $3,000 to $16,000

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aging,
Requirements: First-year admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements. Applicants must meet one of the following: be in the top 25% in their high school graduating class, OR have a 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A"), OR have an ACT score of 22 (24 for non-residents), OR have an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for non-residents). Note that ASU does not require ACT or SAT scores for undergraduate admission. If submitted, they may be used for admission and to confirm competency in math and English.
Department: College of Health Solutions
Concentration: Community Health, Community Services, Advocacy and Social Policy, Communication Sciences, End-of-Life Care, Family Studies, Health Care Administration, Pre-Health, Transborder Chicana/o & Latina/o Studies
Description:
The BS program in aging is a comprehensive, multidisciplinary program designed to equip students with a deep understanding of the aging process from various perspectives, including social, psychological, biological and policy-related aspects. It focuses on the challenges and opportunities associated with an aging population.

The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, such as gerontology, health and aging, cognitive changes in later life, social policies affecting older adults, and ethical considerations in elder care.

The program provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary for careers in fields that serve older adults, such as health care, social services, policy-making and research. Graduates are prepared to contribute to the well-being of the aging population, addressing its diverse needs and promoting healthy and active aging.

This program provides students with a strong foundation in understanding aging. It includes a series of core courses with a variety of electives to choose from and a for-credit internship to gain real-world experience.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agribusiness,
Department: W. P. Carey School of Business
Description: The agribusiness industry is a dynamic sector of the global economy. It is composed of a diverse set of private, public and nonprofit firms and organizations that provide inputs to production agriculture; produce, process, distribute and sell food, fiber and bio-energy products and services at the wholesale and retail levels; and provide financial and information services to the sector. The agribusiness program provides students with strong academic preparation in business, management and finance principles and in applied economics. The quantitative and analytical skills that students develop are highly valuable and readily transferrable to other sectors of the economy.
ScholarshipType: New American University merit-based scholarships, need-based aid, private donor scholarships and external scholarships

ProgramName: Agricultural Business and Management
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year students must also meet one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class; 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A"); ACT score of 22 for Arizona residents (24 for nonresidents); SAT score of 1120 for Arizona residents (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: Morrison School of Agribusiness, W. P. Carey School of Business
Description: The BS program in agricultural business prepares students for careers in the dynamic and complex global food and agriculture industry. The curriculum provides a solid foundation in business management and economic principles for a successful career in the management, marketing and financing of ag-related businesses. In the rapidly evolving global and technological environment of the 21st century, the BS program in agricultural business provides students with the entrepreneurial and leadership skills to make complex business decisions. Students learn to apply economic principles and business management skills to solve problems in the food and agricultural industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Air Traffic Management,
Requirements:
To be admitted to the air traffic management program, students must meet the following admission requirements in addition to the university's first-year student admission requirements:

1. minimum 1140 SAT combined evidence-based reading and writing plus math score or 22 ACT combined score or 3.00 minimum ABOR GPA or class ranking in top 25% of high school class

2. Admission may be granted with one deficiency in no more than two of the competency areas. Deficiencies in both math and lab science are not acceptable.
Department: The Polytechnic School
Description:
The BS program in air traffic management provides students with a strong foundation in aviation studies along with an understanding of all facets of the air traffic control system. Students take courses in air traffic control, aviation meteorology, flight operations, aviation safety and human factors.

Graduates are prepared for careers in air traffic control and a variety of other aviation management roles.

The air traffic management program is an FAA-approved Collegiate Training Initiative program, which allows graduates to be recommended to the FAA for hire into air traffic controller positions.

In addition, students have the option to complete flight training requirements to become professional pilots. Flight training courses are offered via a partnership with a local FAA-approved flight provider. Students are responsible for the costs of flight training, which are in addition to and separate from ASU tuition and fees.
Accredidation: The air traffic management program is an FAA-approved Collegiate Training Initiative program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in American Indian Studies,
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in American Indian studies is a multidisciplinary program focusing on the historical and contemporary experiences, perspectives and life ways of the Indigenous peoples of North America. The curriculum challenges students to consider new perspectives and worldviews.

Students learn how to analyze complex issues within a framework of Indigenous-centered knowledge, with an emphasis on tribally-driven, community-engaged research and partnerships that seek to advance tribal sovereignty and self-determination.

This program is based in American Indian studies, one of the leading Indigenous studies programs in the nation. It provides students with a strong foundation in a wide range of fields, including:

*   American Indian law and federal policy
*   community development
*   economic and political development
*   education
*   environmental justice
*   history
*   language and cultural revitalization
*   philosophy
*   religion

The curriculum's strong methodological emphasis prepares students for careers in tribal leadership, law, policy and administration as well as a range of public and private sector jobs in business, education, government and health care.

The program provides excellent preparation for graduate studies in American Indian studies and other social sciences, such as:

*   anthropology
*   history
*   political science
*   sociology

It also offers a solid foundation for professional schools in business, education, law, medicine and social work.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies,
Requirements: First-year student admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year student admission requirements.
Department: New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences
Description:
The BA program in American studies gives students the opportunity to explore the complex interplay of race, gender, class and other forms of social difference that have shaped American culture, both past and present.

Students investigate the ways in which various forms of culture and expression, from film and popular music to political rhetoric and legal documents, reflect, reinforce and sometimes challenge prevailing ideas about American identity.

Core courses provide students with foundational knowledge in American studies and critical training in cultural analysis. Students then go on to tailor their degrees by choosing from a rich menu of cross-listed courses offered by American studies and a host of other programs across the university.

Students are trained to analyze cultural texts of all kinds, to become more sophisticated readers and writers and to understand the historical contexts of American culture and experience. This training offers excellent preparation for graduate programs in the humanities and social sciences and for professional programs in law and education. The critical thinking, writing and research skills students develop can be adapted to a variety of careers in business, journalism, education, public service, politics and more.

ProgramName: Animal Behavior
Department: New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences
Description:
The BS program in animal behavior prepares students for careers working with animals in a variety of settings such as conservation, research and animal welfare, as well as for graduate school in animal behavior or related disciplines (e.g., ecology, evolution, psychology, biology, etc.) and professional schools (e.g., veterinary medicine).

Students in this program are provided an interdisciplinary perspective on animal behavior, learning from faculty experts across multiple ASU academic units (School of Life Sciences, Department of Psychology, School of Social and Behavioral Sciences). Students gain a broad background in the sciences, with core classes on the mechanisms and evolution of animal behavior and electives in specialized topics in animal behavior (e.g., animal communication, social behavior, behavioral endocrinology, canine behavior, primatology). Students also are provided with hands-on experience by completing at least one animal behavior research experience, either in the field or in a laboratory setting. This offers students the opportunity to work in research laboratories with faculty experts in animal behavior.

ProgramName: Animal Health
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The animal health, BS program is designed to meet all the prerequisites for application to a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine program. It differs from other preveterinary majors by including animal nutrition, animal physiology, anatomy and diseases in the curriculum. The program provides the general background in biological and physical sciences needed for advanced study in animal physiology, animal science and veterinary medicine.

The animal health curriculum gives students the opportunity to learn about many species, from livestock and poultry to companion animals and even some exotics. Students are encouraged to use electives to broaden their experience with animals.

Students who are interested in a preveterinary course of study should consider this major and are encouraged to visit the Preprofessional Advising Office website for more information regarding entrance to a veterinary program.
ScholarshipType: Academic achievement, financial need or chosen major

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology,
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a complete ASU application and fulfill ONE of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class; 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = 'A'); ACT of 22 (24 for nonresidents); SAT of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents). First-year applicants should select an additional major when applying for admission. For more information on ASU's admission requirements, visit admission.asu.edu/first-year.
Department: School of Human Evolution and Social Change
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts program in anthropology provides a broad-based approach to the study of humanity and human culture. It is designed to provide students with a multifaceted approach to the evolution of human biology and culture, to past civilizations and to human diversity around the globe.

Anthropology is holistic in its perspective, drawing from biological and social sciences and from humanities in its research and theory. This allows students to develop an understanding of different cultures and to better understand their own. Students learn about the human experience through classroom studies and research and through work in the field and laboratories.

Students are introduced to the principal subfields of the discipline: archaeology, sociocultural anthropology and physical anthropology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Anthropology,
Department: School of Human Evolution and Social Change
Description:
The Bachelor of Science degree program in anthropology offers students a holistic study of the human condition from a variety of perspectives. It provides students with a strong theoretical background and research skills in anthropology and prepares them for further graduate study as well as careers in the public or private sectors.

Students focus on the scientific dimensions of the discipline through training in the theory and methods of biological anthropology and archaeology as well as through in-depth study of areas such as primatology, human evolution, human osteology, bioarchaeology, dental anthropology, medical anthropology, nutritional anthropology, paleopathology, archaeological method and theory, geoarchaeology, zooarchaeology and lithic analysis. The program also emphasizes advanced statistical methods and laboratory-based research. The BS option is particularly well-suited for those who wish to pursue a pre-health track or careers in forensic science or conservation archaeology.

Students in the BS degree program may elect to pursue a general anthropology track or a more specialized concentration in either anthropological sciences, environmental and social sustainability or medical anthropology.

The school offers unique opportunities for students to work with a range of world-renowned faculty at its research centers, including the Center for Bioarchaeological Research, the Center for Digital Antiquity, the Institute of Human Origins, and the Teotihuacan Research Laboratory. Students can also participate in one of its many summer study abroad programs or archaeological field schools and gain firsthand experience working in the field with leading experts in the discipline. The school also provides a range of laboratory-based opportunities for students to engage in research during the academic year.

The School of Human Evolution and Social Change is a leader in finding innovative solutions to the complex problems challenging the human world. The school's transdisciplinary approach helps its students and faculty understand the human story and provide a unique perspective on the human side of global challenges.

ProgramName: Associate of Arts in Apparel Technical Design,
Requirements: Admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements.
Department: The Design School
Description:
The Associate of Arts in apparel technical design is an intensive two-year program focused on the technical skills of apparel design and construction. The program provides the foundational knowledge required in technical aspects of the apparel industry and prepares students to become skilled professionals in various positions, including technical designer, patternmaker and product developer. Students will gain an understanding of apparel production, from concept to finished product, for the global fashion marketplace. Students will learn the following skills:

- industrial sewing
- patternmaking
- digital patternmaking
- garment construction
- production management
- technical design
- technical flat sketching
- Adobe Creative Suite

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Biological Sciences (Natural Resource Ecology),
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The BS program in applied biological sciences with a concentration in natural resource ecology provides a solid foundation in the biological sciences and teaches students to apply this knowledge to the management of natural resources.

The applied curriculum has a strong foundation in biological and physical sciences, with an emphasis on plant and animal ecology, conservation biology, wildlife management, fisheries management, restoration ecology, and landscape ecology. Students learn both in the classroom and in the field at the Polytechnic campus arboretum, in nearby natural areas such as the Sonoran Desert and the Superstition and San Tan mountains, and on regional field trips.

Graduates of the program work for government agencies, consulting firms, nonprofit organizations and in environmental education and research. The natural resource ecology concentration provides a strong background for students wishing to pursue graduate studies in natural resource management, ecology or conservation biology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Biological Sciences (Pre-Dental),
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The applied biological sciences degree program with a concentration in pre-dental studies is a fast-paced, rigorous, relevant preprofessional program designed for students who want a strong foundation in the biological sciences in preparation for dental school.

The curriculum combines a broad-based approach to the various disciplines in the biological sciences with hands-on, research-based laboratory experiences and an emphasis on the critical-thinking skills needed for success in graduate school and in the dental profession.

Students in this program will complete most prerequisites for dental school as part of their major requirements.

Students complete challenging coursework in topics such as:

anatomy and physiology
biochemistry
cell and molecular biology
genetics

Students also gain in-depth experience in scientific laboratories.

The program features an accelerated block format for its biology courses. Students are immersed in a single subject for three-and-a-half weeks, which facilitates mastery of the material before moving to the next subject. Small class sizes (24 to 48 students per class) offer a personalized and supportive learning environment that encourages high academic achievement.

Students have access to a new, state-of-the-art facility featuring high-tech instrumentation that is unavailable on other ASU campuses.

This program provides excellent preparation for students interested in attending dental school as well as for those who wish to pursue a career in biological sciences or other preprofessional programs, such as pharmacy and optometry.
CostPerCredit: Non-resident: $1,478 per credit hour for 1-6 credits; a comprehensive tuition rate applies for 7 or more credits.
ScholarshipAmount: Merit-based scholarships for non-residents range from $9,000 to $16,000 per year.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Biological Sciences (Preveterinary Medicine),
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The BS program in applied biological sciences with a concentration in preveterinary medicine is a comprehensive, interdisciplinary program of study that allows students to focus on the biological sciences as they relate to animal health. The curriculum provides a strong scientific foundation that includes biology, chemistry, mathematics and physics.

The concentration in preveterinary medicine is tailored to meet the entrance requirements for veterinary school and to provide students with the scientific skills and knowledge required to be a competitive applicant to veterinary school and for a successful career in veterinary medicine or a related animal health field.

In addition to rigorous coursework, the preveterinary medicine concentration requires experiential learning in the form of an internship or undergraduate research. The program also provides opportunities for students to conduct research alongside faculty and to take part in study abroad programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Biological Sciences (Secondary Education in Biology),
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The BS program in applied biological sciences with a concentration in secondary education in biology offers an interdisciplinary curriculum that allows students to focus on biology education at the secondary level. Students are provided with extensive training in biological sciences, including ecology, genetics, cellular and molecular biology and evolution, in addition to pedagogical coursework focused on training students for teaching in a formal secondary school setting.

Students learn how to teach biology through a combination of traditional coursework and hands-on experience in a variety of settings. Through the program's partnership with the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College, students engage in a final semester of full-time student teaching in a secondary classroom. Upon completion of the degree, students are recommended for secondary certification in biology from the Arizona Department of Education.
Accredidation: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Biological Sciences (Sustainable Horticulture),
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The BS program in applied biological sciences with a concentration in sustainable horticulture prepares students for a wide range of careers in horticulture through a solid foundation in plant biology and hands-on training in plant production. Graduates are well prepared to work in a variety of horticultural enterprises, such as plant nurseries, flower and vegetable production facilities, landscaping companies, and botanical gardens and arboreta, or to seek advanced degrees in horticulture, plant biology, plant science and related fields.

The curriculum is focused on the knowledge and skills required for careers in plant production and management, including plant identification and propagation, cultivation of horticultural crops, landscape management, and plant pest and disease management.

Students in this program benefit from the outstanding resources for horticulture at ASU's Polytechnic campus, including a modern greenhouse complex with automated environmental controls; extensive teaching gardens featuring a wide array of plants, including a collection of date palms and other desert-adapted species; and a research farm with facilities for plant production and plant science research.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Biological Sciences,
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Concentration: ['Applied Biological Data Analytics', 'Natural Resource Ecology', 'Preveterinary Medicine', 'Sustainable Biological Systems', 'Sustainable Horticulture', 'Urban and Environmental Entomology', 'Wildlife and Restoration Ecology', 'No Concentration']
Description: The Bachelor of Science in applied biological sciences provides a strong foundation in the life sciences, chemistry, mathematics and physics. A solid understanding of these principles is critical to all areas of biology, whether related to medicine, veterinary science or research. The core of the program addresses cell and molecular biology, ecology and evolution and provides students with skills in critical thinking, writing and problem-solving. This core is supported by extensive hands-on learning experiences in laboratories and field settings, and with independent research opportunities available through faculty research laboratories. Students learn the scientific method and how to interpret and analyze data, making them proficient in using data to create solutions for the changing world. This degree program offers students a choice of several concentrations, allowing them to focus their studies in areas such as pre-veterinary medicine, sustainable horticulture, or applied biological data analytics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Applied Business and Technology Solutions,
Department: W. P. Carey School of Business
Concentration: Food Industry Management, Graphic Information Technology, Information Technology, Operations Management
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in applied business and technology solutions is a fully online program that addresses growing employer demand for a workforce with a broad set of business skills combined with the ability to apply technology in practical, problem-solving ways across a wide variety of industries.

The program's core business courses provide a foundational understanding of data analysis, finance and accounting, marketing and management in the contemporary workplace. In addition to a grounding in business principles, students develop practical technology skills through courses in information technology, graphic design and web development.

The program culminates in a senior-level capstone that applies business and technology knowledge and skills to a specific workplace challenge.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Computing (Cybersecurity),
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The BS program in applied computing with a concentration in cybersecurity focuses on the skills needed to design, implement and manage secure computer networks. Students learn how to build firewalls and other types of network security, and they practice skills for identifying network vulnerabilities and cybersecurity threats.

The curriculum provides a solid foundation in the principles of computing, including data structures, algorithms, computer architecture and object-oriented programming. Coursework provides students with the advanced knowledge they need in information security and data and information management.
Accredidation: The applied computing, BS program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org. Student enrollment and graduation data are available at engineering.asu.edu/factbook/data.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Computing,
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.

First-year admission requirements
A minimum of one of the following:
- top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
- SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)

In addition, all applicants must have the following:
- a minimum of a 3.00 cumulative GPA.
- a grade of "C" or better in all critical tracking courses.
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Concentration: ['Cybersecurity', 'Internet and Web Development', 'Network and Security Administration', 'Project Management']
Description:
The BS program in applied computing provides a solid foundation in the core concepts of computing and information technology. Students learn how to apply problem-solving and critical-thinking skills and knowledge of computing and information technology in a variety of contexts and environments. The program emphasizes the importance of communication, ethics and professionalism, and it addresses a broad range of topics, including networking, security, databases, web systems and project management. Students learn how to configure, integrate and administer computing and information technology systems.

Students develop the skills necessary to work effectively as team members and leaders and gain comprehensive, hands-on experience by completing at least one substantial team-based project.

The curriculum allows students to choose a focus area to further develop their professional interests, such as cybersecurity, internet and web development, or network and security administration.

ProgramName: Associate of Science in Applied Leadership, B
Requirements: Students interested in the applied leadership major must complete an associate of applied science degree from a regionally accredited institution.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description: The Bachelor of Applied Science in applied leadership provides a dynamic, high-quality, accessible degree program that capitalizes on a student's technical education and experience by focusing on the supervision, management and leadership skills needed in a variety of industries. The program builds on a student's foundation of specialized knowledge with advanced coursework in leadership, management and supervision. Students learn to facilitate teamwork, lead projects, resolve workplace conflict, manage change, communicate effectively and supervise diverse teams. The program is designed for students who have earned an Associate of Applied Science degree from a regionally accredited institution. Students who do not possess an AAS degree may be considered for admission if they have significant and extensive work experience in one area of expertise.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics for Life and Social Sciences,
Requirements: Admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a complete ASU application and fulfill ASU's competency requirements: 4 years of English, 4 years of math, 3 years of lab science, 2 years of social science, 2 years of the same second language, and 1 year of fine arts or career and technical education. In addition, students must meet at least one of the following aptitude requirements: top 25% in high school graduating class, 3.00 GPA in competency courses (on a 4.00 scale), an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents), or an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences
Description:
The BS program in applied mathematics for the life and social sciences provides a deep understanding of mathematical concepts and methods that are used to explain and model phenomena in the life and social sciences.

Students develop rigorous skills in mathematical reasoning and advanced problem-solving through a wide range of topics that include:
-calculus
-differential equations
-discrete and continuous modeling techniques
-linear algebra
-numerical analysis
-probability and statistics

Through a flexible curriculum, students have the opportunity to study a variety of related subject areas to fit their specific interests, including:
-animal behavior
-biomedical research
-computational life sciences
-ecology
-epidemiology
-finance
-neuroscience
-social dynamics
-sustainability

The curriculum offers the necessary mathematical and computational tools to model and solve real-world problems. The program integrates coursework in mathematics and life and social sciences to give students the background needed for a successful career in a variety of fields and for advanced graduate studies.

A student pursuing a BS in applied mathematics for the life and social sciences is not allowed to also pursue a BS in:
-actuarial science
-computational life sciences
-mathematics
-mathematics (statistics)
-secondary education (mathematics)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics,
Department: School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences
Concentration: actuarial science, applied mathematics for the life and social sciences, biology, chemistry, computer science, economics, engineering, physics, and statistics
Description:
The BS program in applied mathematics provides a strong foundation in the core areas of mathematics while also exploring connections to other fields. Students learn to use mathematics to solve practical problems in the physical, biological and social sciences as well as in engineering.

A distinctive feature of this program is the required area of concentration, a sequence of courses in a related field chosen in consultation with an academic advisor. This provides students with in-depth experience applying mathematics to another area.

This program offers extensive training in mathematical modeling and computation. Because this is a BS degree program, it has a higher science requirement than the BA program.

Graduates are prepared to pursue advanced degrees in mathematics or in another related field or to find employment in industry, technology or government.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Applied Military and Veterans Studies,
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.

First-year admission requirements
Transfer admission requirements
International admission requirements
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description: The BA program in applied military and veterans studies focuses on the specific historical, cultural, institutional, political, and social issues attendant to the military and veteran communities. The major's curriculum provides an in-depth understanding of the central issues associated with military service and veteran status, especially with regard to health and wellness, social and institutional integration, and family and community. The program's core and related coursework prepares students to become more effective leaders and problem-solvers in the various sectors that interact with service members, veterans and their families. Students gain career-relevant training in leadership, community building and problem-solving, along with the development of the following valuable and transferable skills: communication, information literacy, critical thinking and analysis, social perceptiveness and systems evaluation. Students develop these skills in applied learning environments and research opportunities. Through interdisciplinary coursework and training, the program teaches students about the historical contexts of U.S. and international military conflicts, the psychological consequences of combat and military service, military family dynamics, veteran health issues, and veteran transition and reintegration challenges. Graduates will be prepared to assist service members, veterans and their families through professional roles in government, nonprofit and private sectors, and to pursue a wide variety of graduate and professional degrees.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $15,500 per year (New American University Scholarship)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Nutrition and Health,
Requirements: An applicant for admission to ASU as a first-year student must have completed the ASU competency requirements and have ONE of the following: an SAT reasoning score of 1120 or higher for residents (1180 or higher for nonresidents)*; an ACT composite score of 22 or higher for residents (24 or higher for nonresidents)*; a high school class ranking in the top 25%; a cumulative high school GPA of 3.00 (4.00 = "A") in competency courses. *ASU does not require the writing portion of the ACT or the SAT.
Department: College of Health Solutions
Description: The BS program in applied nutrition and health prepares students with knowledge of the principles of human nutrition and health to pursue careers in a variety of settings. The program helps students understand the vital role that nutrition plays in promoting health and preventing disease throughout the life cycle. Students gain a solid foundation in the biological and chemical sciences in order to better understand the physiological and biochemical functions of nutrients. The curriculum focuses on the practical application of nutrition knowledge to promote positive health outcomes for individuals and communities. Graduates are well prepared to advance their education through graduate study in nutrition or health-related fields, or to enter the workforce in areas such as community and public health, corporate wellness, government agencies, and the food industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Physics,
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Concentration: Business, Computational Physics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics Teaching
Description:
The applied physics BS program combines a professional physics curriculum with substantial experiences in a related field such as engineering, computational science or finance. This program provides an excellent background for a career in a wide variety of engineering and technology-related fields.

The applied physics degree program is appropriate for students wishing to pursue careers in industry or government as well as for those contemplating graduate studies in engineering, computer science, data science, medical physics or other related fields.

Students select a concentration from the list below, with one concentration focused on computational physics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Psychology,
Department: New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in applied psychology provides a broad-based liberal arts education focused on understanding human behavior from a variety of perspectives. It provides students with opportunities to acquire research and other critical thinking skills valued by employers, including in human resources, management, marketing, sales, and in human services and other related settings.

The curriculum features a research sequence culminating in an advanced research lab in which students conduct an original research project, from idea generation through data collection, data analysis and final presentation. The program also offers an internship experience in which students apply their knowledge in a community setting.

Graduates are well prepared for the workforce or for graduate-level work in a variety of fields, such as social work and law.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Quantitative Science,
Requirements:
First-year applicants must meet ASU's general university admission requirements, which includes completion of the ASU competency requirements.

Admission requirements for many majors in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences are higher than university admission standards.

First-year admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements.
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description: The BS program in applied quantitative science provides students with a solid foundation in mathematics and statistics and the skills to apply this knowledge to solve problems in science and technology. Students develop problem-solving, critical-thinking, modeling, and communication skills to answer real-world questions with data and statistics, including in-depth consulting and research experiences that help students develop the skills they need to lead data-driven projects after graduation. The curriculum provides excellent preparation for students interested in careers using mathematics and statistics in business, industry and government, or in further graduate studies in mathematics, statistics and other related fields.
