Students in the film concentration learn by making. They are introduced to the full pipeline of film and media production, from ideation and screenwriting to production (cinematography, directing, sound) to post-production (editing, sound and visual effects).

The concentration provides a strong basis for further study in film theory and history by embedding production courses within a larger media-studies context.

Students can choose to further specialize in areas like directing, screenwriting, producing, cinematography, editing and visual effects. The curriculum focuses on narrative and documentary filmmaking in single-camera and multicamera studio production modes.

Through their study, students gain a solid foundation for careers in the film industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Digital Culture (Graphic Information Technology),
Department: The Design School
Description:
The digital culture BA program with a concentration in graphic information technology is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to focus on how new media is transforming the creation, visualization and consumption of graphics, particularly in cross-media publishing environments, such as print, web and mobile devices. Students learn how media is produced, used and evaluated in a variety of contexts, including fine arts, humanities, social sciences, and science and technology.

The program of study is composed of a broad range of courses from a number of different disciplines and encourages students to experiment and combine different media in new and innovative ways. Students will develop their creativity and critical thinking skills as they learn how to produce, analyze, and manage media for a variety of audiences.

Core coursework provides a solid foundation in the techniques and practices of digital media, and in the critical and theoretical analysis of media and information. The curriculum is project-based, and students are encouraged to be independent learners and to participate in a variety of learning communities, including student organizations, clubs, research groups and labs.

Students in the graphic information technology concentration learn to apply principles of graphic design in web design and publishing, multimedia design and commercial photography and video. The program prepares students for a range of career opportunities involving visual design and technology and provides a strong foundation for a variety of graduate programs.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, College and Departmental, Private Donor

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Digital Culture (Media Processing),
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must meet Arizona Board of Regents minimum academic competency requirements, which include: four years of English; four years of math, including algebra I, geometry, algebra II and a course that requires algebra II as a prerequisite; three years of lab science, with one year each from biology, chemistry, earth science, integrated science or physics; two years of social science, including one year of American history; two years of the same second language; and one year of fine arts or career and technical education.

Additionally, applicants must have one of the following:
- top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents)
- SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: School of Arts, Media and Engineering, Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in digital culture with a concentration in media processing provides students with a foundation in the computing principles and creative practices of digital media. Students gain an understanding of the cultural and social implications of new forms of media creation and expression, and they develop practical skills in media art production. The program offers transdisciplinary coursework in digital media, programming, arts and design, and students use the concepts they learn in class to create their own original artworks and build a portfolio of diverse projects. This program's focus on media processing helps students develop a mastery of audio and visual media computation. The program faculty are leaders in their respective fields, and they bring their expertise and passion to the classroom.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Digital Culture (Music),
Requirements: The Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts requires an additional application for this major. This is a requirement for all applicants, including ASU students wanting to change their major. Prospective students must apply to ASU and the Herberger Institute. Admission to this program requires the submission of a portfolio. All applicants must meet the university's undergraduate admission requirements. First-year applicants must also meet the following criteria: top 25% in high school class, OR 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A), OR ACT score of 22 for Arizona residents (24 nonresidents), OR SAT score of 1120 for Arizona residents (1180 nonresidents).
Department: Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, School of Arts, Media and Engineering
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts program in digital culture with a concentration in music focuses on creating new musical works and tools. Students combine their musical training and creativity with new digital technologies in order to explore and create in areas such as:
algorithmic composition
interactive performance
music and multimedia
new interfaces for musical expression
sound art
sound design
This is a concentration in the Digital Culture, BA program.
In their coursework, students work in a research-based, transdisciplinary and collaborative environment that provides the technical, theoretical and historical foundations for them to create their own digital media work. The core curriculum is a project-based learning environment. Students learn by making.
Additionally, students take courses in a related area and complete their studies with a final portfolio project.
Graduates are prepared for careers in the creative industries and for graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Digital Culture (Theatre),
Requirements: Admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements. To be admitted to ASU, we require you to have completed the 16 competency courses (high school core academic courses). We also require you to have at least one of the following: A top 25% ranking in your high school graduating class. A 3.00 GPA in your competency courses (4.00 = "A"). An ACT score of 22 (or 1120 SAT) for residents. An ACT score of 24 (or 1180 SAT) for nonresidents.
Department: Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, School of Arts, Media and Engineering
Fees: Resident: $12,964/year; Non-resident: $33,592/year (Based on 2023-2024 rates including base tuition and college fees)
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in digital culture with a concentration in theatre is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students for careers in the performing arts as well as in areas that use performance-based approaches and methods, such as film, media performance, motion capture, gaming, performance capture and virtual performance.

The curriculum provides a foundation of courses in theatre history, dramatic literature, acting and directing, performance and design and technology. Students select a series of courses that align with their interests, in consultation with a faculty mentor.

The program culminates in a senior project that involves the creation and production of a live performance or media project. Students are prepared to enter graduate programs in film, performance studies and theatre and to work in professional theatre companies and in the entertainment industry.
CostPerCredit: Resident: $996/credit hour; Non-resident: $1,358/credit hour (for part-time enrollment of 1-6 credit hours)
ScholarshipAmount: New American University Scholar Awards range from $2,000 to $12,000 for residents and $9,000 to $16,000 for non-residents.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Digital Culture,
Department: Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, School of Arts, Media and Engineering
Concentration: Art, Design, English, Film, Interdisciplinary Arts and Performance, Media Arts, Music, Theatre
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in digital culture prepares students to be creative thinkers, collaborative leaders and innovative designers of new media.

Students pursuing the digital culture BA degree select one of the following concentrations: art, design, English, film, interdisciplinary arts and performance, media arts, music, theatre.

The concentration allows for in-depth study in a specific arts and design discipline as it is impacted by digital technology and culture. Digital culture faculty are leading experts and researchers in their fields, from responsive environments and experience design to virtual reality and games.

The program is part of the School of Arts, Media and Engineering, a transdisciplinary school where artists and scientists collaborate. Students learn in an environment that values curiosity, creativity, collaboration and discovery, and they graduate prepared for a wide array of careers in the culture and creative industries.

The digital culture program provides a project-based and transdisciplinary curriculum in which students learn by doing. Foundational coursework in computer science, art, design and music provides students with the creative and technical skills to succeed in their future coursework and careers. Students then build upon these skills in advanced coursework and applied projects focused on topics ranging from wearable technology and interactive installations to game design and virtual reality. Throughout the program, students collaborate with peers from a variety of disciplines and with faculty who are leaders in their fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Digital Marketing,
Department: W. P. Carey School of Business
Description:
The BS program in digital marketing provides students with the critical knowledge of marketing in the digital environment. The curriculum offers a solid grounding in business and marketing and a specialization in digital marketing techniques and practices.

The focus is on search engine optimization, social media and mobile marketing, content marketing, web analytics, and marketing automation. Students are trained to use state-of-the-art tools for web and social media analytics and learn how to help businesses create and manage their digital marketing strategies.

Students gain valuable experience through project-based learning. In their final year, they develop a portfolio by developing a social media campaign for a real client as well as a search engine optimization project.

Graduates of this program may become social media marketing managers, marketing analytics specialists or search engine optimization specialists, or they can pursue a variety of other careers in marketing.
Accredidation: All W. P. Carey School of Business degrees are accredited by AACSB International.
CostPerCredit: $1,460.75/credit hour for part-time (1-6 credits) non-resident students

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Disability Studies,
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year students must successfully complete ASU's competency requirements and have at least one of the following:
- Top 25% in high school graduating class.
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A").
- ACT score of 22 for Arizona residents (24 for nonresidents).
- SAT score of 1120 for Arizona residents (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BS program in disability studies provides students with a complex understanding of disability as a social, cultural and political phenomenon. This interdisciplinary degree program draws upon faculty and courses from a wide range of academic disciplines, including history, literature, philosophy, applied behavior analysis, and speech and hearing science, among others.

Students examine the ways in which social values, cultural representations and institutional practices have shaped the experiences of people with disabilities throughout history, as well as the ways in which people with disabilities have shaped their own lives. Students gain a deeper knowledge of the history of disability, disability culture and the disability rights movement. They also gain a deeper understanding of key disability legislation, including the Americans with Disabilities Act, and they learn to think critically about how disability is represented in the media and popular culture.

Graduates are prepared for careers in fields such as disability advocacy, policy, education, health care, social work, rehabilitation, counseling and human services.

ProgramName: Early Childhood and Early Childhood Special Education, BAE
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description: The BAE in early childhood and early childhood special education offers an innovative, inclusive and interdisciplinary approach to early childhood education for children from birth to age 8. The program emphasizes the development of the whole child as well as learning experiences that are relationship-based, culturally responsive, play-based, and family centered. This program is offered with teacher certification. Students in the teacher certification track benefit from a yearlong residency and a professional learning network as part of their program. Students can select to add an English as a second language endorsement for no additional credit hours, helping them become more culturally responsive educators prepared to teach in diverse classrooms. Graduates are eligible to receive an institutional recommendation from ASU for teacher certification in early childhood education (birth to age 8 or grade 3) and early childhood special education (birth to age 8 or grade 3) in the state of Arizona and most other states.
Accredidation: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Associate of Science in Early Childhood Studies, B
Requirements: This program is designed for students who have an Associate of Applied Science in a child development or early childhood education field from a regionally accredited institution. Students without an applicable AAS degree may be considered for admission. Please contact an academic advisor for more information. All students are required to meet general university admission requirements, which are subject to change. Students should view the ASU admission requirements for the most up-to-date information.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The Bachelor of Applied Science in early childhood studies provides a pathway for students who have earned an associate degree in early childhood education to complete a bachelor's degree. Students acquire advanced knowledge of the early childhood field with a focus on leadership, advocacy, and working with diverse children and families.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in early childhood education, including teaching in Head Start or child care programs, providing early intervention services, and serving in an administrative capacity in early childhood programs.

This degree does not lead to teacher certification.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth and Environmental Studies,
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in earth and environmental studies prepares students for careers in which they assess, understand and manage the natural world and our relationship to it. Students learn the fundamental concepts of earth system science and systems thinking; gain proficiency in geospatial and field techniques for observing the environment; and master qualitative and quantitative approaches for analyzing and interpreting environmental data.

The interdisciplinary curriculum addresses the structure and function of Earth's natural systems, including the solid earth, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere, as well as the complex ways that human societies interact with these systems. Students can focus on topics that include earth system science, geological sciences, environmental science, sustainability, water resources, natural resource management and environmental policy. The program is flexible and allows students to choose courses that suit their individual interests and career plans.

A senior-year capstone experience gives students the opportunity to conduct independent research, engage in an internship or study abroad.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration (Astrobiology and Biogeosciences),
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.

First-year admission requirements
Transfer admission requirements
International admission requirements
Department: School of Earth and Space Exploration
Description:
The Bachelor of Science degree program in earth and space exploration with a concentration in astrobiology and biogeosciences is an an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the natural sciences and engineering with a focus on understanding the past, present and future of life in the universe. Astrobiology and biogeosciences are fields that bring together geology, biology, chemistry, astronomy and physics to address questions about the origin of life and its evolution on Earth and to search for life elsewhere in the universe.

The program prepares students for graduate studies and a wide variety of careers in the space industry, environmental consulting, medical science, laboratory research, science education and public outreach.

The curriculum includes a core set of courses in geology, biology and chemistry and advanced coursework focused on topics such as the evolution of life, the search for life in the solar system, and the interactions between life and the environment. Students are required to conduct research with a faculty mentor, which provides them with hands-on experience in the field and the laboratory.

Students should be sure to work with an academic advisor in the School of Earth and Space Exploration to select courses that are right for their career goals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration (Astrophysics),
Requirements:
In addition to the university's general admission requirements, the following must be met: completion of the required high school competency courses with at least a 'C' (2.00 on a 4.00 scale) in each course.

In addition, a first-year applicant must have one of the following:
- top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = 'A')
- ACT: 22 (24 nonresidents)
- SAT: 1120 (1180 nonresidents)
Department: School of Earth and Space Exploration
Description:
The Bachelor of Science degree program in earth and space exploration with a concentration in astrophysics is an appropriate choice for students interested in careers in astronomy, planetary science and space exploration.

Students in this degree program are required to participate in an introductory seminar in their first year of study as well as a senior-level capstone research or design experience.

This program has an optional component of paid, degree-related employment available through its partnership with the ASU Co-op program. An internship may count toward career-focused required or elective credit in the student's degree program. Students are responsible for securing their own internship or co-op opportunities. Career and Professional Development Services is a resource for students. Students should speak with their academic advisor for more information.

Students in this program are well-prepared to pursue careers in a range of science, technology and engineering fields as well as attend graduate school.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration (Earth Sciences),
Requirements:
First-year applicants must have a high school diploma and will also need to meet the following requirements:

Competency requirements:
- Four years of English (composition and literature)
- Four years of math (one year each of algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite)
- Three years of lab science (one year each of biology, chemistry, and earth science or physics)
- Two years of social science (including one year of American history)
- Two years of the same second language
- One year of fine arts or career and technical education

Aptitude requirements:
Meet one of the following:
- Top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A)
- ACT: 22 (24 nonresidents)
- SAT: 1120 (1180 nonresidents)
Department: School of Earth and Space Exploration
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration with a concentration in Earth sciences provides students with a fundamental background in Earth sciences and prepares them for graduate school or a career in the many quantitative subdisciplines of Earth and environmental sciences. These include environmental consulting, resource exploration, economic geology and geochemistry and geophysics.

The curriculum is designed to have the necessary rigor in mathematics, physics and chemistry to enable students to tackle the real-world Earth and space problems of today and the future. Students engage in authentic, research-oriented activities both inside and outside the classroom. They have the opportunity to participate in field trips and can learn to operate a variety of analytical instruments in their courses and through independent study projects supervised by faculty members.
The degree program offers students exceptional opportunities to participate in research with faculty in the School of Earth and Space Exploration who are internationally recognized in their fields. This program produces highly competitive graduates who go on to careers in research and industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration (Exploration Systems Design),
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration with a concentration in exploration systems design is a transdisciplinary degree that provides a deep understanding of space mission engineering and scientific fundamentals. This degree is well suited to students who wish to pursue a career as a systems engineer in the space and defense industries.

Students in this concentration take a series of systems engineering courses offered through the School of Earth and Space Exploration that prepare them to develop and operate complex systems, including space flight hardware, ground-based scientific instrumentation, and scientific data processing systems. These courses use a hands-on, project-based approach, and students spend most of their time working on a team to build and test space flight hardware or to design space missions. Many systems engineering courses are taken with graduate students who bring valuable experience to the student teams. The courses culminate in a senior capstone project course in which the students design, build, test, fly and operate a payload on a high-altitude balloon, sounding rocket or orbital CubeSat spacecraft.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration (Geological Sciences),
Department: School of Earth and Space Exploration
Description:
The geological sciences concentration in the BS program in earth and space exploration focuses on understanding the past, present and future of the Earth and other rocky planets. Students learn to apply the principles of chemistry, physics and mathematics, in combination with modern geological concepts, to understand the solid Earth and to explore its resources. The program's challenging coursework and ample research opportunities prepare students for graduate studies and a wide variety of careers in the energy and mining industries, environmental consulting, government, and K-12 and postsecondary education.

Students in the geological sciences concentration are trained to understand Earth systems and their resources. The curriculum gives students a robust foundation in the physical sciences and a broad background in all core areas of geology. Students can work with faculty on research ranging from the study of active volcanoes and their hazards to the analysis of the geology and composition of other planets. School of Earth and Space Exploration faculty are internationally recognized in their fields, and the school has state-of-the-art analytical, experimental and computational facilities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies,
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. For first-year students, this includes graduating in the top 25% of their high school class, or having a 3.00 GPA in competency courses, or an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents), or an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents). Applicants must also have completed high school coursework requirements: four years of English, four years of math, three years of lab science, two years of social science, two years of the same foreign language, and one year of fine arts or career and technical education. Please note that ASU does not require ACT or SAT scores for undergraduate admission, but scores may still be submitted for consideration.
Department: School of International Letters and Cultures
Description:
The BA program in East Asian studies offers students a broad interdisciplinary perspective on China, Japan and Korea. The program brings together faculty and courses from a wide range of academic disciplines, including anthropology, art history, business, geography, history, languages and literatures, political science and religious studies.

The curriculum allows students to pursue an area of particular interest while also providing a solid foundation of knowledge about the broader East Asian region.

Students are encouraged to develop a high level of language proficiency and to participate in a study abroad program in order to enrich their understanding of the cultures, societies and contemporary affairs of East Asia.
ScholarshipAmount: Merit-based scholarships up to $10,000/year for residents and up to $15,500/year for non-residents.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Economics,
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Concentration: Politics and the Economy, Public Policy
Description:
The BS program in economics provides students with a deeper and more quantitative understanding of economics than is available through the BA program. It prepares students for a wider range of careers in business and government and is especially appropriate for students who wish to pursue a doctorate in economics or an advanced degree in a quantitative business field, such as finance.

A distinguishing feature of the program is its emphasis on the development of quantitative and analytical skills.

The Department of Economics in the W. P. Carey School of Business has an international reputation for its research productivity, with a faculty that produces cutting-edge research in a wide variety of areas, including:

- econometrics
- macroeconomics
- international economics
- industrial organization
- labor economics
- experimental economics
- environmental economics
- health economics
- public economics
- law and economics
- development economics

Many of the faculty have been elected as fellows of the Econometric Society, a distinction of high honor in the economics profession.

The BS in economics is a STEM-designated degree program.
Accredidation: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International.

ProgramName: Educational Studies (Early Childhood Studies), BAE
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE in educational studies with a concentration in early childhood studies offers a pathway for students interested in a variety of careers working with young children from birth to age 8. The program focuses on child development, learning theory and family and community relationships.

Graduates are well-prepared for entry-level positions in a variety of roles within the early childhood field, such as in Head Start and Early Head Start, child care centers, private preschool programs and other organizations that serve young children and their families.

This program does not lead to teacher certification.

ProgramName: Educational Studies, BAE
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year students must have a minimum of one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class; 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A"); ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents); SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE in educational studies is a non-licensure bachelor's degree program that provides a broad foundation of knowledge in education theory and practice. The curriculum focuses on how people learn and how to best facilitate that learning, giving students the skills and knowledge to engage in meaningful work in education-related fields without obtaining a teaching credential.

Students in this program are prepared for a variety of careers in educational settings outside of the traditional K-12 public school classroom, such as in community education, nonprofit organizations and private tutoring companies. This major is also ideal for those interested in education policy and advocacy, and for students who are passionate about learning but who do not intend to become classroom teachers.

Students can customize their degree program by selecting electives to align with their specific interests and career goals. An array of relevant minors and certificates are also available.

ProgramName: Electrical Engineering (Electric Power and Energy Systems), BSE
Requirements:
The Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering have higher admission standards than university admission standards.

To be admitted to an engineering, computer science or construction program, you must meet the following:

- top 25% in high school class
- OR 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A)
- OR ACT: 24
- OR SAT: 1180

All students are required to have a minimum of one year of calculus. It is strongly recommended that students have a physics course.
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The BSE program in electrical engineering with a concentration in electric power and energy systems is focused on the area of electrical engineering concerned with the generation, transmission, distribution and utilization of electric power and the electrical apparatus connected to such systems. This program provides students a rigorous curriculum in electrical engineering combined with focused coursework in electric power and energy systems.

Electrical engineering is a driving force of modern technology. Graduates with a BSE in electrical engineering with a concentration in electric power and energy systems learn how to develop new products or systems that use electricity or electromagnetism and become specialists in generating, transmitting, distributing and utilizing electric power.

The curriculum provides a strong foundation in circuits, electromagnetics, solid-state devices and computers that allow graduates to pursue careers in a wide range of industries.
Accredidation: The electrical engineering, BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Electrical Engineering, BSE
Requirements:
The following is are the admission requirements for this degree program.

4 years math
4 years English
3 years lab science (1 year each from biology, chemistry, earth science, integrated science or physics)
2 years social science (1 year American history)
2 years same second language
1 year fine arts or career and technical education

And one of the following:

top 25% in high school graduating class
3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The BSE program in electrical engineering is a broad-based, flexible program that provides students with a strong foundation in the fundamentals of electrical engineering.

The curriculum provides a thorough grounding in the basics of electrical engineering, including circuits, electronics, electromagnetics, and digital systems. Students learn about the design and analysis of electrical and electronic systems, as well as the application of electrical engineering principles to a wide range of problems.

The program also includes a strong emphasis on laboratory work and design projects, which provide students with hands-on experience in the field.

Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in a variety of industries, including electronics, telecommunications, power systems and aerospace. They are also well-prepared for graduate study in electrical engineering and related fields.
Accredidation: The electrical engineering, BSE program at the Tempe campus is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Elementary Education (Bilingual Education and English as a Second Language), BAE
Requirements:
Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College has higher admission standards than university admission. All students are initially admitted into an exploratory track and must meet the college’s admission requirements to be admitted into an education degree program.

To be admitted to the college, students must have:
- completion of 30 semester hours of transferrable coursework with a cumulative GPA of 2.25; if the student has less than 30 semester hours of transferrable coursework, they must also meet the requirements for first-year students
- completion of the English composition requirement (ENG 101)
- completion of the mathematics requirement (MAT 142 or equivalent)
- submission of a résumé with educationally-related experience
- a valid Identity Verified Prints (IVP) fingerprint clearance card.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Concentration: Bilingual Education and English as a Second Language
Description:
The BAE program in elementary education with a concentration in bilingual education and English as a second language prepares students to work with children in K-8 general education classrooms and to work specifically with children who are English language learners. The program provides teacher candidates with a strong foundation in the professional knowledge and skills necessary to become a successful classroom teacher in a variety of school settings.

The program is specifically designed to prepare teacher candidates for the multicultural and multilingual classrooms of today's schools and fulfills all requirements for the Arizona Elementary Teacher Certificate for grades K-8 as well as the Bilingual and English as a Second Language endorsements.

The professional education component of this degree features a series of courses focusing on child development, teaching methods, English language acquisition, Spanish language and Latino culture, and the needs of exceptional children. Students participate in a number of school-based experiences throughout the program that provide opportunities to apply what they are learning in their university courses to the real world of the classroom. These experiences are structured so that students begin by observing and assisting in a classroom and gradually assume more responsibility for instructing and managing the classroom. The program culminates in a full-time student teaching experience.

For information about the professional education sequence, including the specific courses that students take and the school-based experiences in which they participate, students should visit the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College website at http://education.asu.edu/.

ProgramName: Elementary Education (Teacher Certification), BAE
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE program in elementary education prepares students to teach kindergarten through eighth grade. The program leads to teacher certification in elementary education, grades K-8, in Arizona.

Students also have the opportunity to add an endorsement or an additional certificate to their degree. Coursework in education theory and methods is combined with multiple field experiences in K-8 classrooms throughout the program. Students gain extensive experience working with children in a variety of school settings. Students' professional growth is supported through personalized academic and career advising as well as by expert faculty and accomplished mentor teachers.

The program is offered at four ASU campuses and at sites across Arizona through ASU Local, providing options for students seeking a range of university experiences and learning environments.
Accredidation: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Elementary Education, BAE
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a minimum GPA of 3.00 in order to be admitted to this program. General university admission requirements for first-year students are completion of competency requirements and meeting one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class; 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A); ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents); SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Concentration: Bilingual Education and English as a Second Language, Educating Multilingual Learners
Description:
The BAE in elementary education prepares students to teach first grade through eighth grade. The program combines rigorous, research-based coursework with extensive classroom-based field experiences. These experiences are structured to produce highly qualified, confident and effective elementary school teachers.

Students select from a variety of school settings in which to complete their field experiences, including public, charter, private, urban, suburban and rural schools. These classroom-based experiences are guided by their assigned mentor teacher and a university supervisor. In their final semester, students complete a full-time, student-teaching residency.

Graduates earn an institutional recommendation from ASU to the Arizona Department of Education for teacher certification in elementary education for grades one through eight. This program is available to students at the ASU Downtown Phoenix, Polytechnic, Tempe and West campuses, as well as at several off-campus locations in eastern and central Arizona.
Accredidation: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Emergency Management and Homeland Security,
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year students must have a high school diploma or GED. In addition, new students must meet at least one of the following four requirements: be in the top 25% of their high school graduating class; have a 3.00 cumulative GPA (4.00=A) in competency courses; have an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents); or have an SAT reasoning score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: School of Public Affairs
Concentration: Biosecurity and Threat Management, Community Resilience, Cybersecurity Policy and Management, Emergency Management, Homeland Security, Hazard Mitigation and Resilient Communities
Description:
The BS program in emergency management and homeland security focuses on the management of all hazards and threats that pose a significant risk to people, communities, infrastructure and the nation. These challenges include manmade, natural and technological disasters, as well as terrorist threats. The program's goal is to minimize the impact of these events on individuals, communities and the nation.

The curriculum prepares students for future leadership positions in public, nonprofit and private organizations. The program's core courses provide a strong theoretical foundation in the comprehensive, all-hazards approach to the emergency management and homeland security fields.

Students are provided with a robust practical dimension through which they learn to apply their classroom knowledge to real-world problems. They also are equipped with the analytical and critical thinking skills needed to effectively respond to and manage complex critical incidents.

The program's faculty have extensive professional experience in all levels of government, the private sector and nonprofit organizations. They also are nationally and internationally recognized for their research and expertise in these fields.

ProgramName: Engineering (Automotive Systems), BSE
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The automotive systems concentration in the engineering BSE program focuses on the design and manufacturing of automobiles and on the integration of automotive components into a final product that is efficient, safe and cost-effective. The program places emphasis on hands-on experiences and solving real-world problems in student team environments, including many opportunities for students to participate in national competitions.

The curriculum in the automotive systems concentration covers topics in automotive structures, vehicle dynamics and controls, hybrid vehicle powertrains, advanced manufacturing and alternative fuels. Upon graduation, graduates will have the knowledge and skills necessary to make an immediate impact in the automotive industry.
Accredidation: The engineering, BSE program with a concentration in automotive systems is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Engineering (Electrical Systems), BSE
Requirements:
The Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering have a First-Year Student direct admission policy. This means that students who meet the following requirements are directly admitted into their major of choice:

First-Year Student

1. Meet all ASU admission requirements.
2. Have a 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A").
3. Meet one of the following aptitude requirements:
    * SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
    * ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
    * class rank in top 25%
    * 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")

Students who do not meet the direct admission requirements will be placed in our engineering exploratory program.
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The BSE program in engineering with a concentration in electrical systems focuses on the theme of power and energy systems. Electrical systems are responsible for the generation, transmission and distribution of electric power as well as the design and manufacturing of a large variety of electrical devices and systems, from small-scale integrated circuits to large-scale power generators.

Students learn how to design and build electrical devices and systems, such as:

biomedical devices
communication systems
electric motors and drives
electronic circuits
power generation and distribution systems
remote sensors

The curriculum is hands-on and project-based. Students build on a foundation of mathematics and science to develop analytical skills and learn to design and build real-world systems in a collaborative, team-based environment. This program is offered by the School of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering, part of the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering.
Accredidation: The bachelor's degree program in engineering (electrical systems) is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Engineering (Mechanical Engineering Systems), BSE
Requirements:
This major has higher admission requirements than university admission standards. To be admitted to this engineering program, you must meet the following requirements:

top 25% in high school class OR
3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A) OR
ACT: 24 OR
SAT: 1180
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The BSE program in engineering with a concentration in mechanical engineering systems is focused on the design of mechanical systems. Graduates of this program will be equipped with a fundamental knowledge of mechanics, thermal sciences and design process to create innovative products and services. Coursework covers the following areas: statics, dynamics, solid mechanics, materials, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, design, manufacturing processes and systems analysis. The program is specifically designed to provide students with hands-on labs and state-of-the-art facilities that include advanced equipment, such as wind tunnels, material testing machines, manufacturing systems and 3D printing, enabling them to gain practical skills and experience to meet the needs of the industry.

This program is offered at the Polytechnic campus and offers a practice-based curriculum with a focus on project-based learning. In their final year of study, students are required to complete a senior capstone design project that involves them working with a team to solve a real-world problem for an external stakeholder. The program's proximity to industry in the East Valley of Phoenix provides opportunities for student internships, research and projects.

This program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Accredidation: This program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Engineering (Robotics), BSE
Department: School of Manufacturing Systems and Networks, Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Fees: Arizona resident: $11,948/year; Nonresident: $34,446/year (based on 2024-2025 base tuition rates for the Polytechnic campus).
Description: The BSE program in engineering with a concentration in robotics focuses on the design and development of robots and robotics systems. This interdisciplinary curriculum provides a broad foundation in the science and mathematics of engineering along with hands-on experience in the design and prototyping of modern engineering systems. The courses in the curriculum focus on mechanical design, manufacturing, electronics, control systems and computer science to develop a strong foundation in robotics. The program provides the knowledge and skills necessary to design, develop and implement robotic systems to meet the needs of modern society. Graduates of the BSE in engineering with a concentration in robotics are well-prepared for a variety of job opportunities in the high-demand areas of robotics, automation and manufacturing. Industries served by robotics engineers include aerospace, automotive, national defense, medical devices, agriculture, entertainment, manufacturing and the emerging area of personal robotics.
Accredidation: This program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for an engineering program of a level and scope commensurate with the title of the program.
CostPerCredit: Arizona resident: $996/credit hour (plus fees); Nonresident: $1,436/credit hour (plus fees) (based on 2024-2025 part-time rates).
ScholarshipAmount: For the New American University Scholarship, amounts for new first-year students range from $3,000 to $12,000 for Arizona residents, and $9,000 to $16,000 for nonresidents.

ProgramName: Engineering Management, BSE
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in Engineering program in engineering management provides a foundation of engineering, math, science, business and management, upon which is built the technical skills and business acumen needed to excel in management and leadership roles.

The curriculum is a blend of traditional industrial engineering courses and courses in business and management, covering topics such as supply chain management, project management, quality control, production planning, computer applications and operations research. The program has two focus areas: industrial engineering and software engineering.

Graduates are able to design, implement and manage complex management systems that involve people, materials, information, equipment and energy. They have an in-depth understanding of technology, innovation, and the challenges of a globally competitive market, as well as the ability to improve the quality of goods and services while reducing costs.

The program's educational objective is to produce graduates who are technically competent and business-aware and who are prepared to succeed in a globally competitive marketplace.
Accredidation: The engineering management, BSE program at the Polytechnic campus is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English (Creative Writing),
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in creative writing gives students the opportunity to work with and be mentored by distinguished faculty with national and international reputations.

Students in this program study the art and craft of creative writing in a variety of genres, including:

Creative nonfiction
Fiction
Poetry
Screenwriting
Spoken word and performance poetry
Students read and analyze a wide variety of texts to identify and learn narrative and aesthetic strategies. They apply what they learn as they write and revise their own work. In small workshop classes, students share and critique each other's work and gain experience in craft analysis, collaborative discussion and revision strategies. In addition to gaining a solid foundation in the study of literature, students may also take courses in linguistics, film and media studies or creative writing.

Graduates of this program have all the skills of an English major, including skills in critical reading, analysis and writing, with the added benefit of experience in writing creatively, giving and receiving feedback, and revising their own work for an audience.

This program is also available as an online program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English (Linguistics),
Requirements: First-year applicants must meet ASU's general university admission requirements, which include completion of the following: 4 years English (composition/literature) 4 years math (algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite) 3 years lab science (one year each from biology, chemistry, earth science, integrated science or physics) 2 years social science (including one year of American history) 2 years same second language 1 year fine arts or career and technical education And one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A") ACT: 22 (24 nonresidents) SAT: 1120 (1180 nonresidents)
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts program in English with a concentration in linguistics focuses on the formal study of language in its humanistic and scientific dimensions, including the nature of subconscious linguistic knowledge, the ways in which languages are acquired, the ways in which languages change and vary, and the roles language plays in society and literature.

The concentration includes courses covering the core areas of linguistics (phonetics, phonology, syntax and semantics) as well as courses in a variety of other topics, including:

    historical linguistics
    language acquisition
    language variation and change
    morphology
    pragmatics
    sociolinguistics

Students in the linguistics concentration acquire skills in data analysis, argumentation and cross-cultural understanding. These skills can lead to careers in business, computer science, government, law and teaching, including teaching English to speakers of other languages.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English (Literature),
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a top 25% high school class rank or an unweighted GPA of 3.00 (4.00 scale) in competency courses. Additionally, applicants must have one of the following: an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents) or an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).

ASU does not require SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission. You can choose whether or not to submit your scores. If you submit your scores, they will be used for admission. If you do not submit your scores, you will be required to have a 3.00 GPA in your competency courses.

Admission may be granted with lower scores or a lower GPA if the student has other academic strengths. Students should see the ASU website for complete information on admission requirements.
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, Department of English
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in literature immerses students in the study of literature and culture. Literature is a living art form with a rich history of traditions from around the globe. Those who study literature at ASU explore the ways it reflects, shapes and critiques cultures. Students learn to read with greater insight, to write with greater clarity and grace, and to think with greater critical acumen.

The literature program offers a wide range of courses in English, American and world literatures, from introductory surveys to specialized seminars, including courses on:

classical and medieval literature
digital humanities
ethnic American literature
film studies
global and postcolonial literature
literary history
literary theory
popular literature
Renaissance literature
rhetoric and composition
women's literature

Students can count courses from other departments --- classics, history, philosophy, religious studies, and women and gender studies --- toward the major. The flexibility of the curriculum encourages students to combine a passion for literary study with a wide range of other interests.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English (Secondary Education),
Requirements:
Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College invites first-year, transfer, international and readmitted students to apply for admission. Students should be aware that the professional teacher preparation programs in the college have higher admission standards than general university admission.

First-year admission:
- top 25% in high school graduating class, OR
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A), OR
- ACT score of 22 for Arizona residents (24 for nonresidents), OR
- SAT score of 1120 for Arizona residents (1180 for nonresidents)

In addition, all applicants must meet the university's English language proficiency requirement.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in secondary education prepares students for careers as English language arts teachers in middle schools, junior high schools and high schools. In this program, students develop a broad and deep understanding of literature, rhetoric and composition, linguistics, and adolescent literacy that translates directly into effective and inspiring teaching of the English language arts. Coursework is aligned with the standards of the National Council of Teachers of English and the Arizona Department of Education.

The program is offered by the Department of English in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences in collaboration with Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College.

Professional experiences are an integral part of this program. Students complete a variety of field experiences in which they observe, tutor and teach in middle school and high school classrooms. During the final two semesters, students are engaged full-time in student teaching with an experienced and qualified mentor teacher. The MLFTC Office of Professional Experiences assists in coordinating all placements.

This program prepares students to meet the requirements for institutional recommendation for teacher certification in the state of Arizona.
Accredidation: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English (Writing, Rhetorics and Literacies),
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a high school diploma and are required to meet competency requirements and at least one performance requirement. Competency requirements include 16 core courses in high school (4 years English, 4 years math, 3 years lab science, 2 years social science, 2 years second language, 1 year fine arts or career/technical education). Performance requirements include one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class, 3.00 GPA in competency courses, ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents), or SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in writing, rhetorics and literacies provides a comprehensive education in writing and rhetoric useful for a variety of professions in which written, visual and digital communication are central.

This English program emphasizes the study of writing in a variety of contexts to prepare students for careers in which strong writing, research and analytical skills are essential.

Students in this program explore the history, theory and practice of writing. They develop skills in argument and persuasion, discourse analysis, digital literacies, research methods and the study of writing in a range of public and professional contexts.

Students analyze how texts (written, visual, digital) are produced, how they circulate and how they are received by different audiences in a variety of contexts. They learn to be more effective writers and communicators, preparing them for jobs in industry, government and education as well as graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English,
Requirements:
All students must meet general university admission requirements. In addition to a high school diploma, you must have completed the following high school coursework, called competency requirements:

- Four years of English (composition and literature)
- Four years of math (one year each of algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite)
- Three years of lab science (one year each from three different sciences chosen from biology, chemistry, earth science or physics)
- Two years of social science (including one year of American history)
- Two years of the same second language
- One year of fine arts or career and technical education

To be admitted, students must meet one of the following:
- Top 25% in high school graduating class.
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A").
- ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents).
- SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, Department of English
Description:
The bachelor's degree program in English provides a comprehensive and dynamic curriculum in which students explore the power of language and literature to shape the world.

The program features small classes, award-winning faculty and a great deal of flexibility so that students can focus their studies on what most interests them.

The curriculum also fosters transferable skills that are highly valued by employers in every profession: sophisticated reading and writing skills, critical and creative thinking, strong research abilities and a nuanced understanding of diverse cultures.

The Department of English also offers students the opportunity to earn a bachelor's degree and a master's degree in a shorter amount of time through the 4+1 accelerated degree program. After completing the undergraduate requirements, students in this accelerated program can share up to 12 credit hours between the BA and the MA, thus decreasing the time it takes to earn both degrees.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Enterprise Leadership,
Requirements: The College of Integrative Sciences and Arts degrees are offered to students who meet university admission requirements. General university admission requirements for first-year students include a high school diploma, completion of 16 core competency courses, and meeting one of the following: being in the top 25% of their high school graduating class, having a 3.00 GPA in competency courses, an ACT score of 22 (24.5 for nonresidents), or an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents). Please note that ASU is test-optional and you are not required to submit an ACT or SAT score to be considered for admission to ASU.
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description: The BA program in enterprise leadership is for students who want to develop essential leadership skills necessary for navigating and succeeding in a variety of complex organizational settings, from small businesses to large corporations and from nonprofits to government entities. This innovative program focuses on real-world challenges and problem-solving, equipping students with the tools to inspire, motivate and guide teams toward common goals. Students gain a deep understanding of organizational dynamics, strategic thinking and ethical decision-making, preparing them for impactful careers across various sectors. The curriculum combines theoretical knowledge with practical application, ensuring graduates are well-prepared to lead with integrity and vision in a rapidly changing global landscape. This program is ideal for aspiring leaders who are passionate about making a difference and driving positive change within their organizations and communities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental and Resource Management,
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Concentration: ['Conservation Biology and Ecology', 'International Development and Sustainability', 'Sustainable and Renewable Resources']
Description:
The BS program in environmental and resource management provides students with a science-based curriculum focused on the management of natural resources, including water, land, plants and wildlife. Students learn principles of ecosystem resilience, and they learn how to apply those principles to the management of natural resources in a changing world.

The curriculum is interdisciplinary in nature. Students take courses in chemistry, biology, physics and math as a foundation for a core of classes in environmental and resource management that prepares them for careers in which they are tasked with finding solutions to complex environmental challenges. Students also have considerable flexibility in selecting their upper-division science electives, which allows them to design a more specialized curriculum based on their interests and career goals.

Graduates with a BS in environmental and resource management are well-prepared for a variety of careers in the environmental consulting industry as well as with local, state and federal government agencies responsible for the stewardship of natural resources. They are also well-prepared for graduate studies in a variety of related fields, including ecology, conservation biology, hydrology, resource management and environmental science.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Chemistry,
Department: School of Molecular Sciences
Description:
The BS program in environmental chemistry provides students a strong background in chemistry that is tailored to understanding and solving environmental problems at the molecular level. Graduates are prepared for careers in a wide range of fields, including:

environmental consulting
environmental law
environmental regulations and compliance
hazardous waste management
industrial hygiene
pollution control and remediation
public health
water purification

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Design and Construction,
Requirements:
The Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts recommends the following for prospective students:

a minimum of 1140 on the SAT (evidence-based reading and writing, and math)
a minimum of 22 on the ACT
a minimum of 3.00 cumulative GPA (scale is 4.00 = "A")
a rank in the top 25% of their high school class

First-year applicants must meet ASU's general university admission requirements, which includes completion of the ASU competency requirements.
Department: The Design School
Description: The bachelor's degree program in environmental design and construction provides the skills and knowledge needed to pursue a variety of careers related to building and landscape construction, materials, methods and management, as well as those careers in the area of historic preservation. Students graduate from the program with a Bachelor of Science degree. The environmental design and construction program is composed of two concentrations: construction management and historic preservation.

ProgramName: Environmental Engineering, BSE
Department: School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment
Description: The BSE program in environmental engineering focuses on the scientific and engineering principles needed to protect and clean the environment. Students learn to apply their knowledge of the natural sciences (chemistry, biology, physics) and mathematics to design and operate pollution control and resource recovery systems. The coursework provides a strong foundation in the concepts of fluid mechanics, and water and wastewater treatment, as well as air pollution control, solid and hazardous waste management, and environmental systems modeling. The program provides the technical competence and professional skills to prepare students for a career in environmental engineering. Graduates are prepared for professional practice or for advanced studies. Environmental engineers are involved in a variety of activities that can directly impact public health and the environment. Opportunities for environmental engineers include working in industry, for consulting firms, or in government agencies. The undergraduate program in environmental engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
Accredidation: The undergraduate program in environmental engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science,
Requirements:
First-year applicants must have a high school diploma and meet one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class; 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = 'A'); ACT score of 22 (24 nonresidents); SAT score of 1120 (1180 nonresidents).

In addition, all applicants must meet the following competency requirements: four years of English; four years of math; three years of lab science; two years of social science; two years of the same second language; and one year of fine arts or career and technical education.

Arizona State University is test-optional for most applicants. First-year applicants are not required to submit ACT or SAT scores to be considered for admission. However, some ASU scholarship applications may require test scores.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Concentration: ['Conservation Biology and Ecology', 'Environmental Chemistry', 'Environmental Engineering', 'Environmental Policy and Management', 'Geological Sciences', 'Sustainable Food Systems', 'Sustainable Horticulture', 'Water, Climate and Energy']
Description:
The environmental science BS program provides students with a strong foundation in the sciences to understand environmental problems and the skills to generate solutions. It is designed to develop a generation of leaders to address critical challenges in the environment, including climate change, biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation, and pollution. The curriculum combines a foundation in natural and social sciences with extensive hands-on experience in the field and laboratory and with data analysis to provide students the skills and knowledge needed for a successful career in the environmental sector.

Students in the program also develop strong written and oral communication skills, as well as problem-solving and critical thinking skills.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in consulting, governmental agencies and nongovernmental organizations. The degree program also prepares students for graduate studies in environmental science or a related discipline.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Family and Human Development,
Department: T. Denny Sanford School of Social and Family Dynamics
Description: The BS program in family and human development explores the dynamic and complex nature of human development across the life span within the context of families, communities and society. This program gives students the tools to improve the lives of children, youth and adults with an interdisciplinary approach that combines coursework in psychology, sociology, physiology and education. Through a variety of class formats and out-of-the-classroom learning experiences, students apply what they have learned to hands-on settings in the community. Students learn how to create and implement evidence-based programs in human services agencies and educational settings.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Fashion,
Department: The Design School
Description:
The BA program in fashion is a transdisciplinary program that provides a foundation for students to work in many roles in the global fashion industry, from design and merchandising to marketing and management. The program is housed in the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, with strong connections to the W. P. Carey School of Business and the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication.

This forward-thinking, industry-facing degree program focuses on creative exploration and professional practice, emphasizing the development of an entrepreneurial mindset. Students learn the fundamentals of design thinking, fashion history, materials and technology, and business principles.

Within this flexible curriculum, students pursue a concentration in either fashion design or fashion merchandising.

The concentration in fashion design prepares students for positions in the areas of creative and technical design within the fashion industry.

The concentration in fashion merchandising prepares students for positions within the areas of fashion marketing, journalism, public relations, event management and merchandising.

The curriculum is enhanced by a required internship, study abroad opportunities and student-run ventures, including a student fashion blog, a retail venture and an annual fashion show. The program is committed to developing well-rounded, creative professionals who can adapt to the rapidly evolving global fashion industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film (Film and Media Production),
Department: Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts
Description:
The BA program in film with a concentration in film and media production offers students a broad, liberal arts-based course of study in the cinematic arts. Students are provided the opportunity to study film from a variety of perspectives, including theory, history and practice. The curriculum develops students' creative and critical skills, allowing them to pursue careers as independent filmmakers, work in a variety of roles on film and media productions, or find film-related jobs in areas such as cinematic arts management, film programming, and film and media archiving and preservation.

Students in this program are not required to complete a second language.

Students pursuing this degree will be enrolled in the film and media production concentration, which is housed at the Tempe campus and provides students with a solid foundation of production courses along with the flexibility to pursue an internship, minor or second major of their choice.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film (Filmmaking Practices),
Department: Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, The Sidney Poitier New American Film School
Description:
The BA program in film with a concentration in filmmaking practices is an interdisciplinary degree that gives students a broad understanding of the art, craft and business of filmmaking. The curriculum helps students develop the critical and creative skills to produce compelling media content for a range of platforms and venues.

In this program, students are immersed in a hands-on production environment from their first year. They gain proficiency in all aspects of filmmaking, from preproduction to post-production, including:

- directing
- producing
- screenwriting
- cinematography
- editing
- sound
- production design
- visual effects

Students have the opportunity to make a variety of media projects, including narrative and documentary shorts, commercials, and web series. The school has a state-of-the-art production facility, with editing suites, sound mixing rooms, and a sound stage. Students also have access to a wide range of professional equipment, including industry-standard cameras, lighting and sound gear.

The program is part of the Sidney Poitier New American Film School, which is dedicated to training the next generation of diverse film artists and industry leaders. The school is committed to creating a more inclusive and equitable film industry, and its curriculum reflects this commitment. Students learn about the history and theory of film, with a focus on underrepresented voices and perspectives.

Students have opportunities to network with industry professionals through guest lectures, workshops and internships.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Media Studies,
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The film and media studies program offers a Bachelor of Arts degree that focuses on the history, theory and criticism of film, television and new media. It is an academic, not a production, program.

Students are encouraged to develop a critical understanding of film and media from various historical, cultural and theoretical perspectives. They work with a faculty of national and international standing, and they have opportunities for internships in the film industry and various other media-related institutions.

The curriculum offers a liberal arts education that prepares graduates for a wide range of career opportunities. Graduates are well prepared for careers in film and media criticism, the film industry, arts administration and education as well as for graduate study in film and media.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Finance,
Department: W. P. Carey School of Business
Description:
The BS program in finance provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to work in a variety of finance-related fields.

The curriculum is designed to familiarize students with the institutions, theory and practice of finance. The program provides an understanding of how financial markets and institutions work, how to value and use a variety of financial instruments, and how to assess and manage risk in a variety of settings. Students learn how to analyze financial information and make sound financial decisions that create value.

Students may also complete a certificate in financial planning.

The Department of Finance has strong ties to the local and national business community. Finance faculty members are nationally and internationally recognized for their research. The department provides students with many opportunities to interact with finance professionals. Many student organizations, including the Financial Management Association and the Student Investment Management Fund, bring prominent professionals to campus to speak with students.
Accredidation: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Financial Planning,
Requirements:
First-year admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements.

ASU is committed to helping students thrive by keeping barriers to entry low and funding opportunities high. That is why we have a test-optional admission process for all undergraduate programs.

ASU does not require an application essay or personal statement.

Students who meet the first-year admission requirements below are assured admission to ASU.

For this program, the following are the admission requirements:

Aptitude
* top 25% in high school class, or
* 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A"), or
* ACT: 22 (24 nonresidents), or
* SAT: 1120 (1180 nonresidents)

and

Competency Courses
* 4 years English (composition or literature based)
* 4 years math (one year each of algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite)
* 3 years lab science (one year each from biology, chemistry, earth science or physics)
* 2 years social science (including one year of American history)
* 2 years same second language
* 1 year fine arts or 1 year career and technical education
Department: W. P. Carey School of Business
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in financial planning provides students with the necessary knowledge and skills to assist individuals and families with a variety of financial needs, including investment selection, retirement and estate planning, and risk management.

Graduates of the financial planning program find career opportunities in the fast-growing industry of personal financial services. The BS program in financial planning is a CFP Board-registered program. Graduates are eligible to sit for the national Certified Financial Planner™ certification examination. The program combines rigorous financial planning coursework with an applied learning component. Students gain hands-on experience by volunteering in the community to deliver financial literacy workshops and by working in paid and unpaid internships with financial services firms. In addition, students have opportunities to participate in professional development activities, to meet industry professionals and to network.
Accredidation: The BS program in financial planning is a CFP Board-registered program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Food and Nutrition Entrepreneurship,
Department: College of Health Solutions
Description:
The BS program in food and nutrition entrepreneurship is a unique business-focused nutrition program designed to prepare students for careers that create innovative, evidence-based solutions for health.

Students learn about food, nutrition, business, communication and leadership. They gain essential knowledge and skills that will enable them to contribute to new and existing businesses in the rapidly growing health and wellness industry.
