Operations managers are problem-solvers who are interested in data and analysis and how to improve business processes.

Operations management and analysis graduates work in supply chain management, purchasing, logistics, consulting, quality management, project management and many other fields.
Accredidation: All W. P. Carey School of Business degrees are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Organizational Leadership (Project Management),
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a command of English and demonstrate evidence of likely success in a challenging academic curriculum. ASU looks for students who are involved and who have contributed to their schools and communities. Admission requirements for this program are the following: top 25% in high school graduating class OR 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A") OR ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents) OR SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in organizational leadership with a concentration in project management offers an innovative, interdisciplinary curriculum with a focus on leadership theory, project management principles and techniques, and data-driven decision-making. Students benefit from an outcomes-based approach that includes a unique curriculum of eight-week courses that are fully online and taught by professional faculty from a variety of academic and professional backgrounds. Students are prepared to become versatile and resourceful project management professionals with the strong leadership and communication skills needed in today's global organizations, whether they are in the public, private or nonprofit sector.

The project management concentration focuses on providing students with the knowledge and skills needed for careers in the growing field of project management. The curriculum is aligned with the Project Management Body of Knowledge developed by the Project Management Institute and covers all the major areas of project management: scope, time, cost, risk, quality, communications, human resources, procurement and integration management.

In this program, students develop skills in project planning and scheduling, budgeting, resource allocation, risk management, and communication. Students learn how to effectively lead and motivate teams and manage project resources.

In the program's capstone course, students participate in a real-world project, which allows them to apply the knowledge and skills they have gained and to build their professional portfolio. This program prepares students for the Project Management Institute's Certified Associate in Project Management examination.

This program is offered by the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Organizational Leadership (Veterans, Society and Service),
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description: The BA program in organizational leadership with a concentration in veterans, society and service focuses on developing the knowledge and skills for effective leadership in a variety of public, private and nonprofit settings, with a distinctive emphasis on understanding the veteran population. Students develop key communication, leadership and management skills for success in leading contemporary organizations. Students also gain a deeper and more thorough understanding of the unique strengths veterans bring to the workplace as well as the needs they and their families often have in health care, social services, and educational and career transitions from the military. The organizational leadership degree program is offered by the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts. The college's faculty is composed of nationally and internationally recognized scholars whose teaching and research focuses on the complex task of leading modern organizations in an increasingly diverse and globalized world. The program is ideal for veterans, active-duty military and military-family members as well as for those who aspire to work with and advocate for this growing and important segment of American society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Organizational Leadership,
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The BA program in organizational leadership provides an interdisciplinary education focused on theories and practices of leadership and leadership development. The program prepares students for leadership roles in a variety of public, private and nonprofit settings. The program also helps students who are already in leadership positions to be more effective.

Students in the organizational leadership major learn to:

apply leadership theories to real-world challenges
lead and manage organizational change
build teams and manage conflict
make ethical decisions
communicate effectively

The curriculum builds upon a liberal arts foundation and combines coursework from the social sciences and humanities. All students complete an internship or applied project, integrating classroom knowledge with practical experience.

The program's interdisciplinary focus cultivates intellectual flexibility and the critical thinking skills needed to analyze complex problems from multiple perspectives. The program's emphasis on ethics, communication and diversity prepares graduates who can help organizations thrive in an increasingly complex and diverse global marketplace.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Parks and Recreation Management,
Requirements:
First-year applicants must meet ASU admission requirements.

In addition, first-year students must meet the following requirements:

minimum 3.00 GPA in ASU competency courses (4.00 = "A")
Department: School of Community Resources and Development
Description:
The BS program in parks and recreation management prepares students for a variety of careers in the management of parks, recreation and tourism services and is designed for students interested in improving the quality of life within communities and for visitors. Parks and recreation management professionals work to provide and manage outdoor recreation experiences, sport and recreation programs in the community, and tourism and special event opportunities.

Students are prepared with a strong foundation of knowledge in management, marketing, leadership and programming. Throughout the curriculum, students gain career-relevant experience through hands-on learning in the classroom, in the community and in professional settings.

Graduates of the parks and recreation management program are well-prepared for entry-level professional positions and advancement to mid-management and upper-management positions within public, nonprofit and commercial organizations. Areas of emphasis in this major include park and recreation administration, sport management, tourism management and community recreation.
Accredidation: The BS program in parks and recreation management with a concentration in therapeutic recreation is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs upon the recommendation of the Committee on Accreditation of Recreational Therapy Education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Pharmacology and Toxicology,
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description: The BS program in pharmacology and toxicology provides a strong background in basic sciences, including chemistry and biology, as well as in-depth coursework and hands-on laboratory experience in pharmacology and toxicology. Students are introduced to the effects of chemicals on biological systems and learn about the discovery, development and regulation of drugs. They learn to identify and characterize the effects of drugs and other chemicals on the body, from the molecular and cellular levels to the organ systems and whole organism levels. They are exposed to a broad spectrum of topics including disease mechanisms and drug action, drug metabolism and disposition, mechanisms of chemical-induced toxicity, regulatory processes, and the application of modern research methods to solve pharmacological and toxicological problems. Through hands-on laboratory courses, students learn modern techniques used in the fields of pharmacology and toxicology. With a strong foundation in pharmacology and toxicology and basic sciences, graduates of this program are competitive for a wide range of graduate programs.
ScholarshipAmount: $3,000 to $16,000 per academic year for non-residents

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy (Morality, Politics and Law),
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts program in philosophy with a concentration in morality, politics and law provides a solid foundation for careers in law, public service, and public and private administration by focusing on the values and principles that underlie and justify political and legal institutions.

Students in this program benefit from close interaction with faculty who have international reputations for their scholarship. They develop their skills in reasoning, analysis and argumentation through challenging coursework, research opportunities and a variety of philosophy-related extracurricular activities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy,
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a minimum of a 3.00 cumulative GPA (on a 4.00 scale) in their competency courses OR be in the top 25% of their graduating high school class OR have an SAT reasoning score of 1120 (for Arizona residents) or 1180 (for nonresidents), or an ACT composite score of 22 (for Arizona residents) or 24 (for nonresidents). ASU is test-optional. You can be admitted to ASU and most degree programs without an ACT or SAT score if you have a 3.00 or higher GPA in your competency courses.
Department: School of Historical, Philosophical and Religious Studies
Concentration: Morality, Politics and Law, Science, Nature and Mind
Description: The philosophy bachelor's degree program teaches students to think clearly and critically about the most important questions of human existence. In philosophy classes, students examine classic texts, analyze arguments and write their own reasoned arguments. These skills are valuable to a wide range of graduate studies and professional careers.

ProgramName: Physical Education, BAE
Requirements:
Arizona State University requires the following for admission:
- completion of the ASU competency requirements
- a minimum 3.00 cumulative GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- a high school diploma
- one of the following:
    - a top 25% ranking in your high school graduating class
    - ACT score of 22 for Arizona residents (24 for nonresidents)*
    - SAT score of 1120 for Arizona residents (1180 for nonresidents)*

*ASU does not require the writing portion of the ACT or SAT.

In addition, new students must meet the following admission requirements for this degree program:
- attend an information session
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE in physical education prepares students for careers as physical education teachers in K-12 schools.

The program emphasizes a holistic approach to physical education, focusing on developing physically literate individuals who have the knowledge, skills and confidence to enjoy a lifetime of healthful physical activity.

The program's curriculum is aligned with national and state standards for physical education and provides students with a strong foundation in the areas of motor development, exercise physiology, biomechanics, curriculum development and instructional strategies.

Students also gain extensive hands-on experience through a variety of field experiences in local schools, culminating in a full-time student teaching internship during their final semester.

Graduates are prepared to meet the requirements for teacher certification in Arizona and other states, and are equipped with the skills and knowledge to create and implement effective physical education programs that promote lifelong health and wellness for all students.
Accredidation: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics (Astrophysics),
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The BS program in physics with a concentration in astrophysics offers a strong foundation in classical and modern physics, and it provides specialized knowledge in astrophysics. This foundation prepares students for graduate study in astrophysics and related fields and for a wide range of careers in industry, data science, technology and education.

Specialized courses in astrophysics include theoretical astrophysics, observational astronomy and cosmology. The program focuses on active learning, with small classes and research opportunities, and provides exceptional career and academic mentoring by faculty members.

In addition to a rigorous and challenging curriculum, physics students often choose to enhance their education by getting involved in a wide variety of activities available at ASU, including the Society of Physics Students, research opportunities with faculty in the department, and science outreach programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics (Professional),
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must successfully complete ASU's competency requirements:

- Four years of math (including algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite)
- Four years of English
- Three years of lab science (one year each from biology, chemistry, Earth science or physics)
- Two years of social science (including one year of American history)
- Two years of the same second language
- One year of fine arts or career and technical education

In addition to the competency requirements, students must also meet at least one of the following aptitude requirements:

- Top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents)
- SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description: The BS program in physics with a concentration in professional physics is designed for students with a keen interest in physics who plan to pursue graduate studies in the field or who plan to work as professional physicists in industry or government. Students gain a rigorous grounding in both classical and modern physics, learning to apply physical principles to the solution of problems. They learn to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data collected. They also learn mathematical methods and the use of computers to solve physics problems. The concentration in professional physics is excellent preparation for graduate studies in physics, as the required coursework closely follows the guidelines of the American Institute of Physics. This includes advanced courses in electricity and magnetism, quantum mechanics and thermal physics, plus an advanced laboratory course. Graduates of this program may also elect to seek employment as physicists. They may find entry-level positions in industry or government in areas related to applied physics and engineering, such as aerospace, electronics, computation and energy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics (Secondary Education),
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description: The BA program in physics with a concentration in secondary education is a comprehensive program for students who wish to become high school physics teachers. The program provides a broad introduction to the fundamental principles of physics, with advanced coursework in mechanics, electricity and magnetism, and quantum physics. The program has been developed jointly by the Department of Physics and Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College. Graduates from this program receive an institutional recommendation from ASU to the Arizona Department of Education for certification as a secondary school teacher in physics. The program is part of a concerted effort by the physics department to respond to the urgent need for well-qualified high school teachers of physics and to the President's call for 100,000 new STEM teachers nationwide.
Accredidation: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics,
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. For first-year admission, this includes completion of high school competency courses (4 years English, 4 years math, 3 years lab science, 2 years social science, 2 years second language, 1 year fine arts or career and technical education) with no deficiencies. Additionally, applicants must meet at least one of the following: be in the top 25% of their high school graduating class; have a 3.00 GPA in competency courses; have an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents); or have an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in physics program provides a comprehensive survey of the main fields of physics in a flexible curriculum. It is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in a field where a strong background in physics is desirable or for students who wish to become certified as secondary school physics teachers.

The physics BA program gives students a solid foundation in physics while allowing them the flexibility to explore other academic areas. For example, students may wish to combine their studies in physics with preprofessional training in medicine, law or business; with a second major in philosophy, English or another liberal arts field; or with in-depth study in a technical area such as computer science, biology or engineering.

Students are not required to complete a senior-level capstone course; however, they may choose to complete an undergraduate research project or thesis as an elective.

For students who may be interested in a career in medicine, ASU offers a preprofessional health program. Pre-health professions advisors are available to help students prepare for medical school and other health professions.

Students who may be interested in a career in law can take advantage of the pre-law advising services at ASU. Students are encouraged to meet with a pre-law advisor early in their academic career and throughout their undergraduate experience.

Students who are interested in pursuing teacher certification should meet with their academic advisor to ensure that all requirements are met.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics,
Requirements:
Arizona State University has a set of requirements that all students must meet for admission. Admission requirements for many majors in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences are higher than university admission standards.

First-year admission:
- top 25% in high school graduating class OR
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A") OR
- ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents) OR
- SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)

Admission to this program requires a higher level of preparation than university admission. Students who meet university admission requirements are placed in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences exploratory program and need to successfully complete key courses to be placed into this degree program.
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in physics is designed to provide a broad and solid education in classical and modern physics with an emphasis on the theory and application of physics in the 21st century.
The program is suitable for those planning careers in research in physics or a related field (with a graduate degree); in secondary education; or in industry, including the aerospace, data science, defense, electronics, energy, medical, semiconductor and technology sectors.
In addition to the fundamental physics curriculum, students can participate in research projects in areas such as biophysics, cosmology, elementary particle physics, condensed matter and materials physics, nanoscience, and physics education. Many of these projects are in collaboration with faculty in other departments on campus and at other institutions and national laboratories. The Department of Physics offers research opportunities not only at the Tempe campus but at the Downtown Phoenix campus as well, through the Center for Biological Physics. Undergraduates will find access to state-of-the-art facilities for their research, such as the LeRoy Eyring Center for Solid State Science, the Center for Biological Physics and several facilities in the Biodesign Institute.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science,
Department: School of Politics and Global Studies
Description:
Political science is the study of governments, public policies and political processes, systems and political behavior. It is a social science dealing with the theory and practice of politics and the analysis of political systems and political behavior.

The BA program in political science provides students with a broad and systematic understanding of the political world and the skills to think critically, communicate effectively and conduct research. Students learn how to ask and answer important questions about politics, both domestic and international. They study how governments and political systems are structured and how they function, and they learn about the political ideas that have shaped the world.

Students may focus their studies on particular subfields, including:
- American politics
- comparative politics
- international relations
- political theory

In addition to a broad liberal arts background, this program provides students with the opportunity to develop skills in oral and written communication, as well as in critical and analytical thinking.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Political Science,
Department: School of Politics and Global Studies
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in political science program provides students with the research tools to study social phenomena. This degree program prepares students to become leading researchers in a variety of social science fields.

The BS degree program in political science is recommended for students who want to develop more advanced quantitative analysis skills, especially those interested in continuing on to graduate school in political science, in data-driven careers in politics, government or the private sector, or in some law degrees where these skills are particularly helpful. The program prepares students to become leading researchers in various fields, with high-level skills in social science statistics, mathematics and research design.

The School of Politics and Global Studies is a dynamic and engaged community of scholars who are nationally and internationally recognized in their fields. Students learn from and work with faculty members who are leading experts on topics such as:

campaigns and elections
conflict and human rights
international relations
Latino politics
law and society
political theory
women and politics

As an integral part of the school, the BS program in political science prepares students with the tools they need to be socially aware, critically thinking and engaged citizens.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Population Health,
Department: College of Health Solutions
Description: The BS program in population health provides students with the foundational skills and knowledge needed to improve the health of populations and promote health equity for all. Students learn the foundational skills and knowledge needed to improve the health of populations and promote health equity for all. They also develop the skills needed for evidence-based practice and decision-making by completing coursework in areas such as epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy, program planning, global health, and social and behavioral health. This comprehensive curriculum offers students the opportunity to examine the complex factors that influence human health and disease and to explore methods for protecting and improving the health of entire populations. The program can provide the foundation for graduate studies in public health or for medical, dental or pharmacy school, and it can prepare students for a wide range of career opportunities in the health care industry. Students interested in applying for graduate school or professional programs such as medical, dental or pharmacy school are strongly encouraged to connect with their academic advisor to discuss the specific courses they should take.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Preveterinary Medicine,
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The BS program in preveterinary medicine is a comprehensive, four-year undergraduate course of study that combines coursework required for admission to a college of veterinary medicine with in-depth study of animal structure and function. Students develop a strong background in biology and chemistry and advanced coursework in anatomy, physiology, nutrition, immunology and other animal-related subjects.

The curriculum is ideal preparation for students who want to become veterinarians but who also may decide to pursue graduate or professional school opportunities in other health-related areas or careers in the biotechnology or animal health industries. The degree program includes all of the required coursework for admission to most colleges of veterinary medicine.

Students who wish to pursue a career in veterinary medicine may do so with a variety of undergraduate degrees. Because admission to veterinary college is not guaranteed and is extremely competitive, students are advised to choose a degree program that offers a strong background in the sciences and offers a variety of career options.

This major is eligible for the Western Undergraduate Exchange program at a reduced tuition rate. The WUE tuition rate is available to students from Alaska, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oregon, South Dakota, Utah, Washington, Wyoming, Guam, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI).

This program is offered by the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts at the Polytechnic campus.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Professional Flight,
Requirements:
First-year applicants must meet ASU's general university admission requirements. In addition, The Polytechnic School has higher admission standards than the university minimums.

First-year admission requirements for this program are the same as the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering admission requirements.

First-year students must meet one of the following:
- top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
- SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: The Polytechnic School
Concentration: Air Transportation Management, Unmanned Aerial Systems
Description:
The BS program in professional flight prepares students to become professional pilots. Graduates earn a commercial pilot certificate with multi-engine and instrument ratings.

The program focuses on developing the aeronautical knowledge, skills and flight proficiency needed for a career as a professional pilot. Students learn to fly in the most technologically advanced aircraft and simulators available. The program meets the requirements for a restricted airline transport pilot certificate. With a restricted ATP, a pilot needs only 1,000 flight hours to be eligible to fly for an airline, compared with 1,500 hours otherwise required. Additionally, a graduate of ASU's professional flight program earns the commercial pilot certificate in as few as 450 flight hours versus the standard 1,500 hours it could take from other flight schools.

Students have the opportunity to make valuable contacts with industry professionals. Upon completion of flight training, students can apply for certified flight instructor positions with ASU's flight provider, AeroGuard Flight Training Center.

Graduates are prepared for careers as professional pilots.
Accredidation: This program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Professional Science (Applied Physics),
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description: The BS program in professional science with a concentration in applied physics provides a unique alternative to traditional degree programs in science. This innovative program combines a strong core in the major with professional skills in communication, computation and workplace practices. Students are trained in the fundamentals of physics and in how to apply their knowledge to technology-based careers. In addition to technical proficiency, students gain critical workplace skills such as project management, business fundamentals and leadership.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Professional Science (Environmental Technology and Management),
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.

First-year admission requirements:
one of the following:
- top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A)
- ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)*
- SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)*

*ASU does not require ACT or SAT scores for admission. You may voluntarily submit test scores for review.

Transfer admission requirements:
one of the following:
- 3.00 transfer GPA (4.00 = A)
- Arizona General Education Curriculum (AGEC)
- associate degree

All transfer students must have a cumulative transfer GPA of 2.50 (4.00 = A) and some majors have higher requirements. Please see the ASU transfer guide for more information.
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The Bachelor of Science degree program in professional science with a concentration in environmental technology and management is an innovative, interdisciplinary program that combines a science background with professional skills to prepare students for a variety of careers in the technology and management sectors of the environmental industry.

The program provides students with the critical skills and knowledge needed to address the complex environmental challenges facing society.

The curriculum combines courses in life and physical sciences, technology and engineering, management, and leadership. Students learn from faculty in the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts and Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering who are experts in their fields and have extensive experience in the environmental industry.

Students have opportunities to gain hands-on experience through internships and research projects with industry partners and government agencies.

Graduates are well prepared for careers in a variety of fields, including:
-environmental consulting
-environmental health and safety
-natural resource management
-sustainability

Graduates are prepared for career paths in industry and governmental agencies as well as for admission to professional science master's programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Project Management,
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a command of English and demonstrate evidence of likely success in a rigorous university curriculum, as demonstrated by completion of the following competency courses with a grade of 'C' (2.00 on a 4.00 scale) or better:

English - 4 years (composition/literature based)
Math - 4 years (one year each of algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite)
Laboratory Science - 3 years (one year each from three different subject areas: biology, chemistry, earth science or physics)
Social Science - 2 years (including one year of American history)
Foreign Language - 2 years (same language)
Fine Arts or Career and Technical Education - 1 year
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The BS program in project management provides students with the knowledge and skills needed for careers managing projects in a variety of industries.

Students learn the entire project life cycle, from initiation and planning to execution, monitoring, controlling and closing. The curriculum covers a wide array of courses, including:
-agile project management
-change management
-cost and schedule control
-leadership
-procurement
-quality management
-risk management

The program provides a deep understanding of project management principles, tools and techniques. Students are prepared to plan, execute and oversee projects to successful completion, making them valuable assets to any organization.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in project management is accredited by the PMI Global Accreditation Center for Project Management Education Programs (GAC). The GAC is the world's leading specialized accrediting body for project management and related degree programs, attesting to the quality of the ASU degree program and its graduates.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology,
Requirements: Admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements. Applicants are required to complete high school competency courses (4 years English, 4 years math, 3 years lab science, 2 years social science, 2 years foreign language, and 1 year fine arts or career and technical education). In addition, applicants must meet at least one of the following aptitude requirements: be in the top 25% of their high school graduating class, have a 3.00 GPA in competency courses, an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents), or an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents). Please note that ASU is test-optional and does not require ACT or SAT scores for admission.
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in psychology provides a strong foundation for a variety of careers and for the pursuit of graduate studies in psychology and other professional fields. The degree program emphasizes the development of critical and analytical thinking skills.

Students learn about the science of behavior and mental processes through active learning and mentored experiences in research labs and community settings. Many psychology majors also complete a second major, a minor or a certificate in other areas, such as family and human development, business, or justice studies, to expand their skills and career options.

ASU's Department of Psychology is an award-winning department that has been recognized by the American Psychological Association for its undergraduate program. The program provides the opportunity to explore many areas within psychology through a wide variety of research areas and courses such as:

Social Psychology
Clinical Psychology
Cognitive Psychology
Developmental Psychology
Behavioral Neuroscience
Abnormal Psychology
Memory and Forgetting
These courses represent the major areas of psychological science.

Students interested in pursuing a graduate degree in psychology or a related area are strongly encouraged to gain research experience by working in one of the psychology department's more than 30 research labs. The Department of Psychology's website has a search tool for finding research opportunities.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychology,
Department: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in psychology program provides a strong foundation in the concepts and methods of the science of psychology.

Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes, from the level of the nerve cell to the level of the group. The BS program offers a more extensive background in the foundational areas of psychology and a more comprehensive quantitative and research methods sequence than does the Bachelor of Arts program. The degree is excellent preparation for graduate study in psychology as well as other professional fields, such as law and medicine.

Psychology majors gain experience in analyzing, interpreting and synthesizing information in a scientific manner. These are skills that are highly valued in many work environments.

The bachelor's degree in psychology is a popular undergraduate major. Many students choose to combine their study of psychology with another major or minor. Psychology graduates are employed in a wide variety of work settings. Many jobs require specific skills and knowledge in a specialized area, such as applied behavior analysis, and students should check with a departmental advisor for details on specific career-related course sequences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Administration,
Requirements:
First-year student admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements. For a complete list of requirements, visit the admission requirements page.

In addition, students must meet the following guaranteed admission requirements: top 25% in high school graduating class OR 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A) OR ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents) OR SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).

ASU is test-optional. First-year applicants may be admitted to ASU and to this program with a 3.0 or higher GPA in competency courses.
Department: School of Public Affairs
Description:
The BS program in public administration is intended for students who are interested in a career in public service. The program prepares students with the knowledge and skills necessary for management and leadership positions in government and nonprofit organizations.
The curriculum requires courses in a number of public service-related areas, including:

leadership and management
public policy
public finance
urban studies

The curriculum prepares students to solve public problems and to pursue and advance in a public service career. Coursework focuses on the knowledge and skills that are most useful to public service professionals, and students learn to critically analyze and creatively respond to the challenges of governance. Students also develop an appreciation for the ethical dimensions of public service and the importance of professional integrity.
The program is offered by the School of Public Affairs, part of the Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Health,
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must possess a high school diploma and meet one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class, 3.00 GPA in competency courses, ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents), or SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).

In addition, students must complete the following course requirements with a minimum grade of "C" (2.00 on a 4.00 scale): one year of high school biology, one year of high school chemistry.
Department: Edson College of Nursing and Health Innovation
Description:
The BS program in public health prepares students to promote and protect the health of individuals and communities.

Students learn how to analyze and understand the complex factors that influence the health and well-being of individuals, families, communities and populations and develop skills to promote health equity and prevent disease, injury and disability.

The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the five core disciplines of public health:
biostatistics
environmental health
epidemiology
health policy and management
social and behavioral sciences

Students take coursework on topics such as:
global health
health communication
health disparities
health education and promotion
program planning, implementation and evaluation
research methods

Throughout the program, students gain real-world experience through an internship, which provides a valuable opportunity to apply their knowledge and skills in a public health setting.

Upon graduation, students are well prepared for careers in a variety of public health fields, such as:
community health
environmental health
global health
health communication
health education and promotion

They are also well-prepared for graduate studies in public health and related fields, such as health care administration, medicine and public policy.

Graduates of this program may be eligible to sit for the national credentialing exam to become a Certified Health Education Specialist. The CHES exam is offered by the National Commission for Health Education Credentialing and is the only accredited credential in the health education and promotion profession.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Policy,
Department: Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions, School of Public Affairs
Description: The BS program in public policy teaches students the skills to understand, analyze and influence public policy at the local, state and national levels. Students learn to critically evaluate policy arguments, research and data; conduct policy analysis; and communicate effectively about policy issues orally and in writing. The curriculum integrates a strong foundation in public policy with analytical courses in economics and research methods as well as a policy concentration of the student's choice. Graduates are well-prepared for a variety of careers in which they can make a difference in their communities and in leadership positions in government, nonprofit organizations and the private sector.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Public Relations and Strategic Communications,
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements.

Freshmen are admitted to the university as pre-journalism and mass communication students and must complete a minimum of 24 credit hours at ASU with a minimum 3.00 GPA to be admitted into the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication.
Department: Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication
Description: The BA program in public relations and strategic communications provides a comprehensive understanding of how to be an effective communicator in a variety of business, media and nonprofit organizations. Students in this degree program learn how to communicate effectively with diverse audiences and to create and sustain the quality of relationships that an organization needs to succeed. The program also provides skills in managing internal and external communications programs using traditional and new media. Students learn how to respond to and manage crises and to become innovative problem-solvers. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in professional ethics, media law, theory and research. All students are required to complete a professional internship prior to graduation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Service and Public Policy (Emergency Management and Homeland Security),
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.

ASU programs that are NCAA compliant for student-athletes are designated as such on the NCAA Eligibility Center website.

The following is a list of required competencies:
- four years of math
- four years of English
- three years of lab sciences
- two years of social sciences
- two years of the same second language
- one year of fine arts or career and technical education

Also, a student must have one of the following:
- top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
- SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: School of Public Affairs
Description:
The BS program in public service and public policy with a concentration in emergency management and homeland security offers an innovative, interdisciplinary curriculum. It draws on the expertise of faculty in the School of Public Affairs and from a variety of other academic units across ASU.

The curriculum combines a foundation in public service and public policy with specialized courses in emergency management and homeland security and electives drawn from related disciplines. The program prepares students for leadership and management roles in public, private and nonprofit organizations through the study of topics that include:

all-hazards emergency management
comparative disaster management
critical infrastructure protection
cybersecurity policy and management
disaster planning and preparedness
disaster response and recovery
ethical issues for emergency managers
health and medical issues in emergency management
homeland security policy and administration
information technology in emergency management
introduction to public service and public policy
terrorism
The coursework prepares students for challenging leadership positions within the public safety disciplines of fire services, law enforcement, and emergency medical and health services. Students gain the critical-thinking skills and understanding necessary to excel as leaders who must address the challenges of disaster response and recovery.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Service and Public Policy,
Requirements: Admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a minimum of a 3.00 cumulative GPA.
Department: School of Public Affairs
Description:
The BS program in public service and public policy prepares students for careers in the public sector, including in government and nonprofit organizations. Students gain insight into public policy and the issues public and nonprofit managers face, from human resources and budgeting to policy analysis and ethics. Students learn to develop and implement policy and deliver public services effectively and ethically in a diverse and dynamic society. Students acquire an understanding of the structure and function of the public sector, the skills required for success in public service and the values characteristic of public service.

Core coursework in public policy and management provides the foundation for students to develop specializations in areas of individual interest.

The BS program in public service and public policy also offers a concentration in emergency management and homeland security. The concentration prepares students with the knowledge and skills necessary for a career in emergency management and homeland security. Students develop competence in the management of all types of hazards and disasters through the study of planning, mitigation, response and recovery. A wide variety of elective courses in criminal justice, social work, public affairs, geography, communication, sustainability and other areas are available to support and enrich the curriculum.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Real Estate,
Requirements:
The W. P. Carey School of Business has competitive admission requirements, separate from and in addition to university admission requirements. This program may have waiting lists for qualified students.

First-year student admission:
- top 8% of high school graduating class, OR
- 3.60 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A"), OR
- ACT: 26, OR
- SAT: 1260

All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.
Department: W. P. Carey School of Business
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in real estate provides an overview of the tools and concepts used for real estate decision-making.

The program is designed for students who want to develop a broad-based knowledge of business with a specific understanding of real estate markets, law, finance and appraisal. Students are prepared to become leaders who create value in the real-estate development, investment, and lending industries.
Accredidation: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Recreation Therapy,
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. For first-year students, this includes completion of high school competency requirements and meeting one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class; 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A"); ACT score of 22 for Arizona residents (24 for nonresidents); or an SAT score of 1120 for Arizona residents (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: College of Health Solutions
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in recreation therapy program at ASU is designed to prepare competent, entry-level recreational therapists with the knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to become leaders in the field and successfully complete the national exam. The program curriculum is specifically aligned with the requirements of the National Council for Therapeutic Recreation Certification.

The recreational therapy profession seeks to improve the quality of life for individuals with disabilities, injuries or illnesses through active treatment. This is achieved using a systematic approach called the therapeutic recreation process, which includes assessment, planning, implementation, evaluation and documentation. Recreational therapists are active, creative and compassionate professionals who use recreation activities and other life experiences to help people make the most of their lives --- physically, mentally, emotionally and socially.

The program requires students to complete a supervised, professional internship in the final semester of the program. Faculty members assist students in obtaining an internship that fits their desired career path.
Accredidation: The recreation therapy program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs upon the recommendation of the Committee on Accreditation of Recreational Therapy Education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies,
Requirements:
First-Year Admission: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences expects all students to meet the following requirements for admission.

top 25% in high school graduating class
OR
3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
OR
ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
OR
SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)

Transfer Admission: To be admitted to this major, students must have a minimum cumulative transfer GPA of 2.50 and have completed one or more of the following courses.

ENG 101 or ENG 102
a course that satisfies the L requirement
a course that satisfies the MA requirement
a course that satisfies the SB or HU requirement
a course that satisfies the SG or SQ requirement
Department: School of Historical, Philosophical and Religious Studies
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in religious studies is the undergraduate degree program in the academic study of religion.

The curriculum focuses on the critical, analytical and cross-cultural study of religions. Students learn to see religions as complex and historically dynamic traditions, involving texts, rituals, social institutions, and material cultures, which have shaped, and in turn been shaped by, their historical and cultural contexts.

The curriculum covers the major world religions (Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam and Judaism) and also newer, smaller-scale or little-known traditions as well as non-religious meaning systems.

In addition to a broad comparative overview of religious traditions, students also develop expertise in one tradition or a particular theme. Students learn diverse approaches to the study of religion, from fields such as:

anthropology
history
philosophy
sociology

They gain strong research and writing skills, and they learn to think critically about complex texts, practices and social formations. The degree offers a basic foundation in the study of religion that can lead to graduate study or to a wide variety of careers.

ProgramName: Robotics, BSE
Department: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in Engineering in robotics program is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students to meet the challenges of designing and developing the intelligent systems of today and the future. Students will develop foundational knowledge in computer science, data structures, mathematics and the physical sciences, with strong hands-on experience in the design, development, construction and application of robotic and autonomous systems, including control systems and machine learning.

Through an integrative, experience-based curriculum, students will gain experience in the end-to-end design of robotic systems, as well as an appreciation of the social and ethical aspects of these technologies. Students who complete the BSE in robotics will be prepared for work in the increasingly interdisciplinary field of robotics, where expertise in both hardware and software is critical. The curriculum provides breadth and depth across the core areas of robotics (sensing, reasoning and acting) while also enabling students to pursue specialized interests in a specific area.

This program is offered by the School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence.
Accredidation: The robotics BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Russian,
Department: School of International Letters and Cultures
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts program in Russian offers students a solid foundation in the Russian language, with a focus on all four language skills (speaking, listening, reading and writing), and combines it with the study of Russian literature, culture, history, politics and film.

In addition to the skills gained through the study of a foreign language, literature and culture, which are highly valued by employers, students develop the strong intercultural communication and critical thinking skills needed to thrive in an increasingly interconnected and diverse world. Graduates are prepared for careers in a wide range of fields, including education, government service, journalism, national security, nongovernmental and nonprofit organizations, and translation and interpretation.

The program offers a diverse selection of Russian language, literature and culture courses. All Russian majors are strongly encouraged to participate in one of the study abroad programs available in Russia and other Russian-speaking countries.

ProgramName: Secondary Education (Biological Sciences), BAE
Requirements:
Admission requirements for many majors in the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College are higher than university admission standards.

First-year applicants must meet Arizona State University's first-year admission requirements. Among those requirements, the following are the most critical:

First-year applicants must have a complete high school curriculum, and applicants must meet at least one of the following:
- be in the top 25% of their high school graduating class
- have a 3.00 cumulative GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A)
- have an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents)
- have an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)

In addition to the university first-year admission requirements, all applicants to the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College must complete an intellectual curiosity essay.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in biological sciences prepares students to become middle school or high school science teachers. Students learn how to be effective teachers and how to develop and evaluate curriculum and instructional materials.

The program combines coursework in biology and other sciences with courses in the theory and practice of teaching. Teacher candidates learn how to plan lessons, manage a classroom and assess student learning. They are taught how to foster a learning environment in which all students, including those from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds, can succeed.

Extensive field experiences in a variety of school settings give students the opportunity to practice their teaching skills and connect what they are learning in their university classes with the realities of the classroom. The program culminates in a full-time clinical experience (student teaching).

Graduates are recommended for teacher certification in Arizona to teach biology in grades 6 through 12.
Accredidation: This program, which is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation, leads to teacher certification in the state of Arizona.

ProgramName: Secondary Education (Chemistry), BAE
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in chemistry prepares students to teach chemistry in grades seven through 12. The program is a collaboration between the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College and The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Students complete subject matter coursework in the partner college and teacher preparation coursework in the Teachers College.

Graduates of this program earn an institutional recommendation from ASU to the Arizona Department of Education for teacher certification in the state of Arizona in chemistry, grades 7-12.

All students must meet the requirements for Arizona teacher certification. This includes extended field experiences (teacher residencies) in a variety of settings appropriate to the student's chosen content area and grade level. Students should see the academic advisor for information on completing requirements for teacher certification.

ProgramName: Secondary Education (Earth and Space Sciences), BAE
Requirements: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College admission requirements are the same as university admission requirements. First-year applicants must meet one of the following: top 25% in high school graduating class; 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = 'A'); ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents); SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents). Admission requirements for transfer students are a 2.50 cumulative GPA for less than 24 transfer hours or a 2.00 cumulative GPA for 24 or more transfer hours.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in earth and space sciences prepares students to become middle school and high school earth and space sciences teachers.

Coursework in this Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College program emphasizes the content knowledge and pedagogical skills needed to be a highly qualified teacher, including research-based teaching strategies and methods. The coursework is integrated with extensive field experiences in partner districts, culminating in a full-time student teaching internship.

Upon completion of the program, students are prepared to teach a variety of earth and space sciences subjects, including:
- astronomy
- geology
- meteorology
- oceanography

Students who complete this program earn a bachelor's degree and an Arizona teaching certificate in secondary education, 6-12, and a structured English immersion endorsement, K-12. This program is also offered as a fast-track option for eligible students, allowing them to complete both their undergraduate and master's degrees in education in four and a half years.
Accredidation: All educator preparation programs in the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College are accredited by the Association for Advancing Quality in Educator Preparation. ASU is also accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.

ProgramName: Secondary Education (English), BAE
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements.

First-year applicants must have a complete ASU application for admission, including all transcripts and required application fee.

First-year admission requirements:

one of the following:
- top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- ACT: 22 (24 nonresidents)*
- SAT: 1120 (1180 nonresidents)*

*Arizona residents who attend a regionally accredited high school and rank in the top 25% of their graduating class are assured admission to the university. They are not required to submit ACT or SAT scores.

All students, including transfer students, must be in good academic standing to be admitted to this program.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in English prepares students to teach English in grades 6-12. The program emphasizes the knowledge, skills and dispositions needed to be an effective teacher of English in a multicultural society.

Coursework focuses on knowledge of the subject matter, the learner and learning, and curriculum, instruction and assessment. Students learn about the English language and how to analyze literature as well as how to teach reading and a wide range of types of writing.

This secondary education program includes professional experiences in a variety of school settings, including a full-time student teaching internship. The professional experiences, which are integrated with the coursework, provide students with a rich, hands-on experience of working with students from various cultural, linguistic and socioeconomic backgrounds.

All coursework is taken in a sequential manner.

Arizona teacher certification for grades 6-12 is awarded upon successful completion of the program. The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College provides a teaching certification officer who is a liaison to the Arizona Department of Education and who is able to provide information on the certification process.
Accredidation: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Secondary Education (History), BAE
Requirements:
Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College has higher admission requirements than university admission standards. All students are initially admitted into education exploration until they meet the Teachers College requirements.

First-year student admission:

top 25% in high school graduating class OR
3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A) OR
ACT: 22 (24 nonresidents) OR
SAT: 1120 (1180 nonresidents)
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in history prepares students to teach history in grades 6-12. Students learn to develop curriculum, instruction and assessment materials to meet the needs of all learners in history classrooms, including English language learners and students with disabilities.

Students in this program are not required to complete a minor.

In addition to the content knowledge courses in history, students take a range of professional teacher preparation courses grounded in research-based practices, and they spend significant time in partner-district schools working with mentor teachers and students. The program culminates in a full-time student teaching internship. Upon successful completion of all program requirements, graduates are recommended for teacher certification in Arizona.
Accredidation: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the American Psychological Association and the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Secondary Education (Mathematics), BAE
Requirements:
Admission to the BAE in secondary education requires the following:

4 years English (composition/literature)
4 years math (one year each of algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite)
3 years lab science (one year each of biology, chemistry, earth science or physics)
2 years social science (including one year of American history)
2 years same second language
1 year fine arts or 1 year career and technical education

In addition, students must meet one of the following:

top 25% in high school graduating class OR
3.00 GPA in competency courses OR
ACT: 22 for residents, 24 for nonresidents* OR
SAT: 1120 for residents, 1180 for nonresidents*

*ASU is test-optional. Students may be admitted without a test score.
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in mathematics prepares students to teach mathematics to students in grades seven through 12.

The program offers students rich, discipline-based content knowledge and research-based pedagogical training in a clinically rich teacher preparation program. Graduates of the program are prepared to have a positive impact on student learning and to meet the unique needs of diverse student populations.

Students in this program benefit from the expertise of world-class faculty in Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College. This professional educator preparation program in the college is a model for 21st-century teacher education.

The program includes cutting-edge coursework, extensive clinical experiences and a student-centered environment that is supportive of diversity. Students' coursework is enriched by research and hands-on learning in a variety of school and community settings.

Graduates are recommended for teacher certification in Arizona.
Accredidation: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Secondary Education (Physics), BAE
Requirements:
All applicants must meet Arizona State University's minimum undergraduate admission requirements.

To be admitted to ASU, you will need to be considered proficient in the following competency areas:
4 years English (composition/literature based)
4 years math (one year each of algebra I, geometry, algebra II and an advanced math class for which algebra II is a prerequisite)
3 years lab science (one year each from biology, chemistry, earth science, integrated sciences or physics)
2 years social science (including one year of American history)
2 years same second language
1 year fine arts or career and technical education
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts in Education in secondary education with a concentration in physics prepares students to teach physics in a secondary school setting (grades 6-12).

The program provides students with a broad and balanced curriculum of physics and pedagogy coursework. Students explore the principles of physics and how to translate those concepts into engaging and effective lesson plans.

Students also gain hands-on experience by completing a two-semester student teaching experience in a local school. The program is designed to meet the certification requirements of the Arizona Department of Education.
Accredidation: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

ProgramName: Secondary Education (Political Science), BAE
Department: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College
Description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in political science prepares students to teach political science in grades 7-12.

The program offers a solid foundation for teaching political science in secondary schools. It features a combination of academic work in a content area, professional education experiences and courses leading to institutional recommendation for teacher certification.

The secondary education program is an intensive, cohort-based program that requires students to apply for admission in their sophomore year. All students complete a common core of courses providing a strong foundation in secondary education theory and practice, and they are assigned to a full-year internship in the senior year. In addition, students work with an advisor from the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College to ensure that all requirements for teacher certification are met.
CostPerCredit: Arizona Resident: $857 per credit hour; Nonresident: $1,478 per credit hour

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social and Behavioral Sciences,
Requirements:
First-year applicants must meet ASU's general university admission requirements, which include completion of the following:

Top 25% in high school class
OR
3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = A)
OR
ACT: 22 (24 for nonresidents)
OR
SAT: 1120 (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences
Description:
The BA program in social and behavioral sciences provides students with an integrated learning experience that draws on the social sciences to explain the causes and consequences of human behavior. The program's interdisciplinary approach provides students with a holistic understanding of people and societies. Students take courses in a variety of fields, including communication, economics, history, political science, psychology and sociology, to analyze human behavior and its connection to the broader social world.

Students also have opportunities to work alongside faculty on research projects and to pursue their own research interests through the New College Undergraduate Inquiry and Research Experiences program. The college's faculty are nationally recognized scholars in their fields who are dedicated to excellence in both teaching and research.

In this program, students develop a core set of analytic and methodological skills and then choose a variety of social science electives based on their career goals. These courses prepare students for careers in diverse fields, such as business, counseling, law, public administration and social work.

Students pursuing an undergraduate certificate in social sciences research methods can learn social science research techniques and gain hands-on experience by collecting, analyzing, interpreting and presenting data.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social and Cultural Analysis (American Studies),
Requirements: All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year applicants must have a high school diploma and are required to meet the following: complete a minimum of 16 core courses in high school (four years of English, four years of math, three years of lab science, two years of social science, two years of the same second language and one year of fine arts or career and technical education) and meet at least one of the following: be in the top 25% of their high school graduating class, have a 3.00 cumulative GPA (4.00 scale) in core courses, have an ACT composite score of 22 (24 for nonresidents), or have an SAT combined evidence-based reading and writing plus math score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: School of Social Transformation
Description:
The BA program in social and cultural analysis with a concentration in American studies is an interdisciplinary program focusing on the historical and contemporary formations of American culture. Students in American studies explore how race, class, gender, sexuality and place have shaped American society. Coursework in American studies challenges students to learn and use theories and methods from a wide range of academic fields, including:
cultural studies
history
literary studies
media studies
performance studies
sociology
Students have opportunities for independent research and for internships in museums and other cultural institutions in the Phoenix metropolitan area.
The degree can be used to prepare for a wide range of occupations, including:
cultural programming
education
journalism
law
library science
social justice and advocacy work

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social and Cultural Analysis (Ethnic Studies),
Requirements:
All students are required to meet general university admission requirements. First-year | Transfer

First-year admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements.

Read on to learn more about ASU's admission requirements, dates and deadlines.

ASU is test optional. You are not required to submit an ACT or SAT score for admission to this degree program.
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The social and cultural analysis program provides students with a transdisciplinary and integrated understanding of culture, society and identity.

Students in the program analyze social and cultural phenomena through the lenses of history, theory, cultural production, power and positionality. They examine social constructs such as race, ethnicity, class, gender, sexuality and dis/ability, and they learn to communicate effectively about the critical issues of the day, including privilege, inequality and social justice. The curriculum challenges students to move beyond the classroom to engage in the broader community and practice the skills they learn through research and real-world application.

The social and cultural analysis major consists of a common core of courses that grounds students in the fundamental theories and practices in the study of social and cultural phenomena. The program also offers a number of concentrations in specific fields of study, which gives students the opportunity to choose the courses that most closely match their interests and career goals.

The ethnic studies concentration offers in-depth examination of the social construction of race and its impacts at personal, interpersonal, institutional, societal and global levels. Students analyze racial identity formation and the intersections of race with class, gender, sexuality, nationality, ability and other markers of difference. Students learn the histories and cultures of a wide array of racialized and Indigenous groups to prepare for living and working in a diverse society. Courses examine race and racism through multiple disciplinary lenses from the humanities and social sciences. Students are strongly encouraged to select elective courses from across the School of Social Transformation curriculum and from other disciplines across the university.

Students who major in social and cultural analysis are well prepared to work in a variety of settings where critical analysis, creative thinking, intercultural communication, and a strong sense of social responsibility and civic engagement are valued. The program is also excellent preparation for graduate study in a wide range of academic disciplines and professional fields. A bachelor's degree in social and cultural analysis with a concentration in ethnic studies provides a strong foundation for law school or graduate studies in fields such as the humanities, social sciences, cultural studies, communication and justice studies. This concentration is also valuable to careers requiring a strong liberal arts background with a focus on human diversity.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social and Cultural Analysis (Latin American Studies),
Requirements: This major has no additional admission requirements. Students who are admissible to the university are admissible to this major. To be considered for admission to ASU, first-year applicants must have completed high school competency requirements in English, Math, Laboratory Science, Social Science, Fine Arts or Career and Technical Education, and Foreign Language. Additionally, applicants must meet at least one of the following: be in the top 25% of their high school graduating class; have a 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = 'A'); have an ACT score of 22 (24 for nonresidents); or an SAT score of 1120 (1180 for nonresidents).
Department: School of Transborder Studies
Description:
The BA program in social and cultural analysis with a concentration in Latin American studies offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the peoples, cultures, societies and political systems of Latin America and the Caribbean. The curriculum allows students to develop an area of interest within Latin American studies.

Students have an opportunity to gain global awareness and cross-cultural communication skills that can be applied to many careers.

The program offers unique opportunities to study with outstanding faculty in the U.S. and in Latin America and the Caribbean.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies),
Requirements:
To be admitted to ASU, you must meet the following requirements, or if you are an Arizona resident, you must be in the top 25% of your high school graduating class. You may be admitted with one or more deficiencies in the competency requirements, but the university may require you to make up for those deficiencies.

All students must meet the following competency requirements:
- Four years of math
- Four years of English
- Three years of lab science
- Two years of social science
- Two years of the same second language
- One year of fine arts or career and technical education

And one of the following:
- Top 25% in high school graduating class
- 3.00 GPA in competency courses (4.00 = "A")
- ACT score of 22 for Arizona residents (24 for nonresidents)
- SAT score of 1120 for Arizona residents (1180 for nonresidents)
Department: College of Integrative Sciences and Arts
Description:
The social and cultural analysis program at ASU provides students with the intellectual and practical tools for understanding and engaging with the major social and cultural issues of our time, in local, national and global contexts.

The program combines critical social theory, cultural studies, community-based research and engagement, and innovative curriculum to equip students with the necessary skills to analyze complex social problems and cultural phenomena and to become effective leaders of social change.

Students learn to ask pressing questions about the social world, such as how social inequalities are produced and reproduced, how social identities are created and contested, and how different cultural forms and practices shape our lives and the worlds we inhabit. They develop strong analytical, research, writing and public presentation skills to effectively communicate their ideas to a range of audiences.

The peace studies concentration teaches students to link theory with practice to address the major challenges to peace in the 21st century. The concentration draws from a range of fields, including:

conflict resolution
history
political science
psychology
religious studies
sociology

Students gain understanding of how to engage directly with conflict and its effects and to promote positive change through nonviolent and creative means.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social and Cultural Analysis (Queer and Sexuality Studies),
Requirements: Admission requirements for this program are the same as the university's first-year admission requirements.
Department: New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences
Description: The social and cultural analysis program offers a unique interdisciplinary curriculum that enables students to develop a sophisticated understanding of the complexities of our social world. The concentration in queer and sexuality studies allows students to engage in an interdisciplinary study of sexuality and its importance to human societies and lives in the past and present.
